ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Deep River Town Dock (AKA Deep River Landing)  is a large municipal access pier suitable for fishing and offers excellent views of the River.  Children will especially enjoy watching the Essex Stream Train pass by (seasonally).  Historical marker describes the site's historic and cultural significance.  Nice views of Selden Neck State Park across the River. Parking is limited, and fees to access the site may apply to  non-residents.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: One Thirty Seven Rowayton Avenue Waterfront Overlook
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: One Thirty Seven Rowayton Avenue Waterfront Overlook is a waterfront walkway along the Five Mile River.
Five Mile River Realty is the location of a waterfront walkway along the Five Mile River.

Sono Harbor Associates Waterfront Overlook is a waterfront walkway along the west side of the Norwalk Harbor adjacent to a small marina.  Parking is available at city lot just north of this site on North Water Street.  Visitors can enjoy fishing at SoNo Harbor.  Also, waterfront walkways provide for a scenic stroll.  The SoNo Harbor public access site is located adjacent to a marina so visitors can enjoy the views.
Outside the Maritime Aquarium  there is a pavilion on the water with educational signage.  Visitors can fish from the public access pier.  Visit www.maritimeaquarium.org for more information.

Take a leisurely stroll along the water and observe wildlife at Oyster Shell at Heritage Park.  Educational signs are posted along the walkway and there is plenty of parking.  It is directly adjacent to the Maritime Aquarium Park.
Norwalk River Medical Offices allows access to a section of the Norwalk Harbor Loop Trail along the Norwalk River. Visitors can rest and watch the river from benches near the offices.
Oyster Bend Condos Waterfront Walkway offers a walkway along the east side of the Norwalk Harbor adjacent to a marina.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Shore Pointe Office Building Waterfront Overlook
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Shore Pointe Office Building Waterfront Overlook is a waterfront walkway along the east side of Norwalk Harbor adjacent to a marina.  It includes a wooden walkway adjacent to a bulkhead and bench seating.  This site provides visual access to the Norwalk River only.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Transient Boat Docks and Launch at Veterans Memorial Park
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Transient Boat Docks and Launch at Veterans Memorial Park is a large municipal park with a visitors dock for temporary dock space.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Public Boat Slips and Moorings at Veterans Memorial Park
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Public Boat Slips and Moorings at Veterans Memorial Park is a large municipal park with a boat launch ramp for launching trailered boats only.  Small boats must launch at Calf Pasture Beach.
Thomas Place Estate is a small park located along Wilson Cove with a gazebo.  This is a great place to watch boats at the Wilson Cove Boat Club.
The Plains Island is an island in Norwalk Harbor, accessible by boat only.

Sheffield Island Lighthouse is part of the Stewart B. McKinney National Wildlife Refuge and is owned by the Norwalk Seaport Association.  This historic lighthouse is closed most of the year to protect the many birds that nest along the Island's rocky shore.  This site has become a regular wintering ground for harbor seals.  The Sheffield Island Lighthouse is maintained and operated seasonally as a museum by the Norwalk Seaport Association.  Information available at www.seaport.org.  Accessible by boat only.  Public ferry at Hope Dock, 7 Water Street (May-Sept), call 203-838-9744 or 203-838-9444 for information.

Smith Neck Town Landing provides access to the Back River and Great Island with excellent bird watching. There is a very small parking lot at this site. Signage is provided at this site at the driveway entrance. PLEASE NOTE: At low tide there are only a few inches of water available from the launch to the channel. Check tide tables before visiting Smith Neck Town Landing to launch safely your car-top boat. Sanitary facilities are provided only during the summer boating season.
Launch a car-top boat and explore the Connecticut River also used by anglers and birders..
Visitors to the Canal Road Water Access Area may fish, shellfish . Shellfishing restrictions may apply. See http://www.westportct.gov/index.aspx?page=566 to obtain a shellfishing permit.

Take a walk along the edge of the Saugatuck River at the Waterfront Walkway at 341 Riverside Avenue.  Enjoy marsh views as you observe birds and wildlife.  There are no public access signs at this site so visitors should locate it by the address.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Stoddard Hill State Park Boat Launch
ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Stoddard Hill State Park is a small, 55 acre park in Ledyard. The entranceway of the park leads down to a parking area where the Boat Launch is located.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Recently updated facilities at the Barn Island State Boat Launch include two 80-foot sections of floating dock, one of which will be Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) accessible.  Car-top boaters should use the area marked for canoes/kayaks on the right (west) side of the ramp.  New facilities include a state-of-the-art ramp and improved water depths at the launch.  Fishing is allowed on-site but must not interfere with boating activity.  Some routes leading to this site are posted with boat launch symbol signs, in order to help visitors reach Barn Island State Boat Launch.  Consider visiting the extensive trail system at the adjacent Barn Island Wildlife Management Area after engaging in boating activities.  The trails offer extensive views of salt marshes and Fishers Island Sound.  The trailhead is located on the east side of the upper section of the boat launch parking lot.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This popular launch site, located less than 500 feet from the Great Island Wildlife Management Area, provides visitors with opportunities to explore tidal marshes and a barrier beach. It is important to note, however, that motorized vessels must remain a reasonable distance away from the Great Island Wildlife Management Area upon launching. A water trail map of the Great Island estuary is posted near the entrance of this site's parking lot, and offers descriptions of a car-top boat trail (which would take visitors approximately 1.5 hours to traverse south to Griswold Point and approximately 3 hours in duration to return to the launch for the average kayak or canoe user). The map also introduces the history, flora, and fauna of the area. PLEASE NOTE: Visitors should investigate tide tables before launching boats at this site, due to the extremely shallow depth of water at low tide. Some routes to this site are marked with brown and white boat launch signs.

Grace Salmon Park is a municipal park on the Saugatuck River.  Ample parking at this site provides access to a perimeter trail with park benches.  The large lawn area offers excellent picnicking opportunities.
Small waterfront park on Pawcatuck River near center of Pawcatuck village offers picnic and cart-top boat launch facilities. No boat tie-ups allowed at dock.
Launch a car-top boat and enjoy the scenery.  The site is suitable for birding, fishsing and crabbing.
Waterfront Walkway 285 Riverside is a great site to enjoy views of the Saugatuck River.  There are no public access signs at this site so visitors should locate it by the address.
Waterfront Walkway 299 Riverside is a nice place to walk along the Saugatuck River in an urban setting.  This site connects Waterfront Walkway 285 Riverside and Waterfront Walkway 341 Riverside.

The River House Tavern restaurant provides approximately an eight hundred foot walkway along the water with a small park.  There are no public access signs at the entrance but there are a few along the walkway itself.
Riverside Town Park park provides views of the Saugatuck River where uou can sit in the shade at a picnic table or stroll the waterfront walkway.

Jeanette Egan Park fronts Long Island Sound.  Walkways along the beach offer generous water views. On-street parking is allowed on Compo Beach Rd after Owenoke Park, or there is fee parking at adjacent Compo Beach.

Gorham Island is located on the Saugatuck River right in downtown Westport.  Parking is available in the Parker Harding Plaza, take a stroll across the bridge to Gorham Island or just stroll along the Saugatuck River.
Launch a car-top or trailered boat at the Town of Montville Boat Launch.  There is also an access pier available for fishing.

Pilgrim Landing offers views of Calves island and Baldwin Bridge with a car top launch facility located near a dinghy boat storage rack. There is a small parking area. Parking at this site is restricted to only a few cars. There is no space for a boat trailers. Pilgrim Landing is north of Baldwin Bridge on Route 156 past the Old Lyme Marina.

Sound View Beach offers sunbathing and swimming with shops and places to eat within walking distance. Plan to arrive early since parking is limited.  A small public parking lot and time-limited on-street parking at this site limit the number of visitors to this beach. See 'Site Website' for details. You can legally stroll along neighboring beaches as long as you remain on the wet sand area which is held by the State in "trust” for the public.

Saugatuck River Boardwalk is located adjacent to The Inn and Shops at National Hall.  It has a nice boardwalk along the water.  There is a time limit on parking.  There are no public access signs posted at this site.

Enjoy Village Square Waterfront Walkway by walking along the tidal river and observing the array of waterfowl in this urban setting.  This is a nice place to take a lunch break or for a break during a day of shopping in downtown Westport.  Benches are provided.

This site provides fishing and car-top boating access to the Shetucket River at the site of Norwich Public Utilities hydroelectric dam and fish ladder. The canoe/kayak put-in is a 200 yard portage from the parking area. Norwich Public Utilities offers tours of its Greeneville Dam fish lift at a site on the opposite bank of the River from this site from May 1st through June 30th. To learn more about the fish lift, go to the Norwich Public Utilities web site and follow the links. Be extremely careful near the dam. Fatalities have occurred as a result of those who enter the River who underestimated the power of the currents near the dam. Combined sewer overflow discharges along this segment of the Shetucket River may discharge untreated sewage after rainstorms. Avoid direct contact with river water within 24-hours of rainstorms. To help you reach Greeneville Dam Fishing Area, some routes leading to this site are posted with the brown and white Long Island Sound Access sign.

Kirtland Landing is a small boat launch ramp that provides access to the Menunketesuck River.  The ramp is located approximately two miles upstream from the mouth of the Menunketesuck River.  Parking is limited.
At Whalers Point, enjoy beautiful views of the Farm River and Kelsey Island.
The Shoreline Trolley Museum offers walkways and trolley rides through tidal wetlands on vintage trolley cars (seasonal).

South Bank Open Space is a park adjacent to the Housatonic River where visitors can observe wildlife and other passive activities. There is a small picnic area and pavilion at site. The site is closed from dusk through dawn. Swimming in the Housatonic River is prohibited.

Sunnyside Boat Ramp is  located behind an elementary school.  A pass is required to launch trailered boats. Season passes can be obtained at the City of Shelton Clerk's office at 54 Hill Street, Shelton ($100 non-residents). For questions call the Town at 203-925-8422. Non-motororzed/car-top watercraft do not require a pass but must  park at top of hill from the launch.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: BranHaven River and Farm Properties LLC
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Kelsey Landing provides a bench, from which you can enjoy fine views of the Farm River. Consider visiting  the nearby Farm River State Park after resting at Kelsey Landing.

Clinton Town Marina Boat Launch is located in Clinton Harbor and is adjacent to the Clinton Town Marina.  This  popular launch provides access to Clinton Harbor, the Hammonasset River, and the waters off Clinton, Madison and Westbrook in Long Island Sound.

Mariners Point Condominiums provides an exceptional vantage point from which to watch boats sail Milford Harbor.  The entrance to this site is obscure, located at the end of Trumbull Avenue on the Harbor.  When you arrive at the end of Trumball Avenue, Milford Yacht Club will be on the left and the Mariner's Point Condominiums on the right (there is no sign for Mariner's Point Condominiums).  There is a private property sign on a chain link fence that is part of the Yacht Club, don't be deterred from proceeding. To the right of this sign is an attractive walkway located between tall hedges.  This walkway leads through a lawn area to the beach area that has a sign that says private beach but this sign is incorrect--this is a public access walkway leads to the beach and popular fishing area.

This site provides undeveloped pedestrian access to Sherwood Mill Pond and offers up some pretty views. It is an undeveloped spot but visitors can see some good wildlife, fish, crab or launch their cartop boat to enjoy some time on the pond! Parking is on-street along Hillspoint Rd.

Birdseye Street Boat Launch is an easy to use boat launch at the mouth of the Housatonic River with plenty of parking.  There is also a deck for sitting and viewing the Housatonic River and Nell’s Island.  Launching requires town permit.  Restrooms are portable and only available during the summer.
Bond's Dock is a very popular fishing spot and area for viewing the Housatonic River and Nell’s Island.  Some parking is available on the wharf.

The Dock Shopping Center provides river-front access to the Housatonic River.  Amenities include a large public deck with tables and chairs available to the public, as well as an on-site restaurant, walking path, and large fishing pier.  Ample free on-site parking available.

Oak Street Beach Activity Building is a multi-use activity building adjacent to Oak Street Beach.  It provides a place to rest in the shade and educational displays often related to Long Island Sound.

There is a 100 foot carry to the put-in point.  Poquetanuck is a 2 mile long cove extending northeast from the Thames River.  It offers an excellent opportunity to visit a nearly pristine brackish water wetland, the cove being the most extensive wetlands on the Thames River south of Norwich.  The shoreline is dominated by an attractive mix of conifers and deciduous trees.  Watch for osprey fishing.  Parking for only 4 cars.

This scenic overlook is located on Military Highway south of the Nautilus Memorial entrance.  Overlooking Goss Cove, with unobstructed views of the Thames River and Mamacoke Cove, this parklet contains picnic areas, a scenic walkway and public parking.  Town-owned.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This site, located under the I-95 overpass, offers boaters fine views of the historic Mystic River corridor and is also a popular fishing site. The site is particularly well-suited to small car-top vessel launching. Trailered boat launchers use caution when launching at this site as the ramp and launch are steep and in disrepair. Trailer parking is extremely limited and navigation in parts of the upper Mystic River is controlled by tides.

Located at the end of Main Street on the Noank peninsula, this Town-owned site offers unobstructed views of the lower Mystic River and Mason’s Island.  A small beach and dock area are provided (overnight docking is not permitted).  Limited public parking.
Grand Street Boat Launch provides an alternative, especially for car-top boat launching, to the often crowded Niantic River State Boat Launch.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Located between Avery Point and Jupiter Point, this site offers large and small boat launching, trailer parking and scenic views of Pine Island and Bushy Point.  Floating access pier available at this site.  Public parking provided.  To help you reach Bayberry Lane State Boat Launch, some routes leading to this site are posted with boat launch symbol signs.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Along this segment of the Lieutenant River you can paddle a narrow tidal river while enjoying the sights and smells of nearby Long Island Sound. A turn along a bend in the river might provide a view of a tidal marsh or nesting osprey. From the launch, if you paddle to your right, or downstream, you are a little over 0.8 mile from the Connecticut River. If you proceed left (upstream or inland) from the launch, you have about 2.5 miles of scenic paddling to the limit of small craft navigation. Parking for 6 cars. PLEASE NOTE: This site is for car-top boat launching only. Sanitary facilities at this site are offered only during the summer/fall boating season.

This is a quaint dock with a beautiful view of the water.  Only car-top boat launching is available at this site.  On-site parking for residents only. Parking is available for non-residents when school is not in session at the Old Saybrook Middle School on Sheffield Street, a short walk from the dock.

The Newfield Avenue Boat Ramp provides access to Bridgeport Harbor. This site includes a developed boat-launch ramp with accompanying dock for short-term parking of boats and personal watercrafts. To reach this site follow the brown and white Long Island Access signs. Limited on-street parking only.

Brewster Street Boat Launch provides access to Black Rock Harbor. Minimal on-streetonly  parking available. To access this site follow Brewster Street to Black Rock Harboar. Lauch is adjacent  to Fayerweather Yacht Club. Ramp improvements funded by the Long Island Sound License Plate Grant Fund.
Perrys Green is a small  waterfront park with benches overlooking Southport Harbor.  Limited on-street public parking is available.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Explore the Saugatuck River by launching a trailered boat at the Saugatuck River State Boat Launch or putting in a car-top boat to paddle this scenic tidal river.  Sanitary facilities are provided.  To help you reach Saugatuck River State Boat Launch, some routes leading to this site are posted with boat launch symbol signs.

Located at the end of Crystal Lake Road, just outside the main gate of the U.S. Naval Submarine Base, the Nautilus Memorial offers visitors an opportunity to tour the museum and take a self-guided tour of the world’s first nuclear powered submarine, the USS Nautilus.  There is a picnic area on the grounds with views of the Thames River.  Admission and parking are free.  Federally-owned.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This boat launch affords beautiful views of tidal wetlands along the Branford River. Arrive early because this is a popular location. Branford Harbor, the Thimble Islands, and Long Island Sound are conveniently accessible from this boat launch.

Located at the head of Tomac Cove which separates Stamford from Greenwich, Conair Water Access Area offers great views of this quiet cove where many shorebirds hunt in the shallows.  The tree-lined shorefront is defined by rock outcroppings, tidal wetlands, and intertidal flats.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: Historical Society of the Town of Greenwich
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Bush-Holly House Historic Site is a museum on the National Register of Historic Places.  There is a parking lot for museum patrons.  A tidal river is located across the street and a bench is available for public use.
At Harbor House, you can enjoy the beautifully landscaped access area and view the boating activity along the East Branch of Stamford Harbor.
Community Beach is a small beach along the Five Mile River in Norwalk.  Great place for watching boats.

Sherwood Mill Pond Walkway is an elevated wooden walkway over tide gates.  The walkway provides great views of the Sherwood Mill Pond and  tidal wetlands, Compo Cove, and Long Island Sound.  Bring binoculars to observe the wildlife.  Parking lot on site is restricted to Town residents May to September but metered on-street parking is available nearby on  Hills Point Road.

Milford Landing Marina is located at the head of Milford harbor.  This marina offers transient boat slips that are open to the public and a waterfront path that affords great views of the harbor.  The waterfront path connects to a footbridge that leads to additional public amenities and trails across the harbor. Fishing is allowed across the harbor at Wilcox Park.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Savin Rock Conference Center Water Access
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Savin Rock Conference Center provides benches, telescopes and occasional public art displays.  Interpretive signage is provided on the origins of Savin Rock.  A gazebo is available if you prefer the shade.  Beaches are adjacent to this site.  West Haven provides 3.5 miles of public beach or waterfront park, each with its own amenities or environmental setting.  Beaches from Bradley Point Park to Sandy Point are networked through a 1.7 mile walkway providing pedestrians, bicyclists and roller-bladers a continuous waterfront urban “greenway” experience.  Views of Long Island Sound exist throughout most of the walkway.  Most beach parking lots in West Haven close at 11:30 p.m. although the walkway is open 24 hours, every day.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Four Mile River State Boat Launch
ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Four Mile River State Boat Launch provides visitors with a large parking area and a wide boat launch.  One can observe beautiful views of the Four Mile River marsh and wading birds.  It is recommended that boaters launch at high tide.  To help you reach Four Mile River State Boat Launch, some routes leading to this site are posted with boat launch symbol signs.

Located in the heart of New London and serving as the focal point of the newly constructed linear waterfront park, the pier hosts cruise ships,  fishing, and  offers fantastic views of the Thames River. The accompanying waterfront park includes a 1/2  half mile improved promenade. The  park hosts cultural and arts events throughout the summer and recreational facilities including  public mooring and transient dock space, fishing piers, public art displays and a car-top boat access ramp.
Constitution Park is a small park on Norwalk Harbor across from the Norwalk Maritime Aquarium and a great place to watch vessels plying the Harbor's working waterfront.

The Wastewater Treatment Plant Waterfront Walkway is a publicly-accessible pedestrian walkway along the east side of the Norwalk Harbor. Park on-street and stroll along this scenic walkway that continues North along the river and connects with the public access walkways in front of the Riverwatch Condominiums and the commercial UHaul building. Access to this walkway begins near the Oyster Bend Yacht Club aand Marina, though the docks are reserved for private use. At the end of the walkway, relax on one of four benches overlooking the river or continue on to the connecting public access walkways.

This this narrow sandy beach beach, also known as 'Amtrak Beach,' was given to the Town by Amtrak Railroad. It provides a less crowded alternative to other nearby Town beaches . Parking for the beach is via the adjacent Cini Memorial Park. To help you locate this site follow the brown and white Long Island Sound access signs.

The creative re-use of this area under the Niantic River bridge as a small waterfront park offers views of the Niantic River with interpretive signs describing the Niantic River's shellfishery, past and present. Watch charter fishing boats depart from the park, but be careful not to enter the channel under the bridge where swift currents can be extremely dangerous. This site provides access to the adjacent 'Railroad Beach' the Niantic River Boardwalk's eastern terminus and a fishing pier and a car-top (only) boat launch. Day passes are available at the McCook Point Park lower bath house Monday through Thursday and at all three beaches Friday through Sunday.
Mystic River Scenic Overlook is a nice place to stop and rest when driving along I-95.  It provides nice views of the Mystic River and Mystic Seaport.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Stonington Town Dock Fishing Pier and Memorial
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This site is situated in the  village of Stonington Borough.  Although much of the waterfront property in this village has been converted to residential use, there is still an active marine commercial fishing fleet in the harbor.  An interpretive sign at the pier describes the village's maritime history.  Sailboats are commonly seen racing in this area.  This site provides ample parking near the Town's wastewater treatment facility.

DuBois Beach is located in the picturesque seaside village of Stonington Borough. Enjoy the site’s shallow water-depths, on-site pavilion, and clean, family-oriented sandy beach. The beach’s 265 feet of shoreline fills up quickly so plan to arrive early. Stonington Community Center lifeguards monitor the beach for your safety. Park at the Stonington Point lot at the end of Water Street. A day use permit for the beach can be obtained on-site. It is recommended that visitors contact Stonington Community Center at 860-535-2476 for current fee schedule.

Stonington Point offers panoramic views of Fisher’s Island Sound and is adjacent to duBois Beach and the Stonington Old Lighthouse Museum which offers six rooms full of Stonington historical displays and terrific views of the Sound from the lighthouse tower.  Fishing is also allowed at this site.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This parcel, located on Thames Street at the foot of Fort Street, was once used as a landing for Fort Griswold.  Today it offers views of the Thames River and downtown New London’s waterfront.  There are benches and a grass area from which one can view submarines and commercial and recreational boats as they travel the Thames River.  No parking provided.  State-owned.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This is a large boat launch facility with ample parking, and includes an access pier for fishing.  The Baldwin Bridge State Boat Launch received an award from the State for providing excellent boating access.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: The route to this site is through a residential neighborhood in Madison.  The boat launch provides access to both the East River and Long Island Sound for trailered and car-top boats.  A moderately sized parking area is available.  To help you reach East River Wildlife Management Area, some routes leading to this site are posted with boat launch symbol signs.

Island Bay/Shell Beach is a small coarse sand 'pocket beach' offering beautiful views of Island Bay and recreational boating activity. It is ideal for exploring with small children and for collecting sea shells, shellfishing (with a permit) or a careful swimming/cartop boating venture. The entry point to Shell Beach is located right next to a red barn, and parking is somewhat limited. Do not block the private driveway that passes through the parking area. The water at Shell Beach is difficult to access at low tide but during the low tide, this site provides access to mud flats popular for recreational shellfishing. Consult with the Town of Guilford shellfish commission/health department to ask about required permits for shellfishing.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Water Street Public Dock and Launch
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Located on Water Street in the historic Fort Rachel area of Mystic, this facility includes a small boat launch and dock (no overnight docking allowed).  Limited unimproved parking across the street at Burrows Place.  Town-owned.
Fishing and birding are popular activities at this site.

With a view of the Housatonic River, Caswell Cove Water Access Area offers fishing access and a pavilion where you can enjoy lunch.  Bring your own chairs to enjoy the gazebo.  There is ample parking.
Pratt Cove offers trails for hiking starting from the lot along the river to the south. Throughout the preserve there are beautiful views of the Cove.

Also known as The Seawall, Point-No-Point provides easy parking and a pleasant walk along the beach on the Long Island Sound. Please note that at Russian Beach, to the immediate east of Point-No-Point, only the area seaward of mean high water is open to the public.  Walk along the wet sand area of this beach.
Gus Edson Park is a small park along Holly Pond.  It is a nice place to sit in the sun or shade while you watch shorebirds hunt and ducks and swans paddle along.

Scholes Lane Water Access Area is a very small point of access to the Connecticut River located at the end of Scholes Lane in Essex.  There is a small grassy area that drops towards the water for launching car-top boats.  The shore is rocky.

Essex Town Park is a quiet park located in the center of Essex with views of the Connecticut River and in proximity to shops and restaurants.  The park includes benches and a beautiful lawn that overlooks the river.  Visitors can launch their canoes or kayaks and discover Essex's coves and views.

Essex Town Dock is located at the foot of Main Street, adjacent to the Connecticut River Museum.  The boat launch ramp provides access to the Connecticut River.  This is a perfect location for watching sailboats race inside Nott Island.  Parking is limited.

This small park on River Street overlooks the Niantic River.  Picnic tables and benches provide a pleasant spot for lunch or a place to rest after fishing from a new pier that is expected to be completed summer 2017.
Captain John's Sport Fishing Center boardwalk provides pedestrian access along the Niantic River to the Town dock at Mago Point.

This is a quaint area adjacent to a tidal creek.  A picnic table is available to enjoy lunch while watching wildlife forage in the creek and tidal wetlands.  There is no public access sign posted, and there is parking for two to three cars.
A waterfront walkway along the east side of the Norwalk Harbor is open to the public.
At Pasacreta Park, visitors can walk along the Saugatuck River, bring a picnic lunch, and observe wildlife.  This park also provides fishing access.  Ample parking.
Driftway Water View fronts Long Island Sound.  Suited for bird and wildlife watching.  Benches are provided.
Sammis Street Bridge is a waterfront walkway and bridge located at Farm Creek in Rowayton.  Contact Norwalk Land Trust for more information.

Limited water depths and ramp conditions make this site appropriate for launching small craft only. Do not park vehicles at the launch site. Very limited parking on Isham Street. Alternatively, leave boat at launch and park 6 blocks south at the 4th District Voting Hall at 10 Broadway (7 minute walk from launch). Vehicles parking on Bay street may be towed. No traiilered boat launching. Use Mystic River State Boat Launch, River Road, Groton, on north side of I-95 overpass for trailered boat luanching.
The Bay Street Parklet is a small grassy area with benches adjacent to the Isham Street Boat Launch on the Mystic River.  The site is a nice place to enjoy views of the Mystic River.

This 50 foot wide right-of-way provides public access from Essex Street easterly to the Mystic River.  Because the site is a working shipyard, access is confined to a designated 50 foot wide right-of-way only and a walkway in front of the yacht club building.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Branford High School Car-top Boat Launch
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Branford High School offers car-top boat access to the Branford River. This site can be accessed south of the football field. It is 100 yard boat portage from parking area to River. To be sure that this site is open please call the high school at (203) 488-7291.

Behind the Delamar Hotel, there is a walkway along the edge of the water with views of Greenwich Harbor and Smith Cove.  There is a small area with benches that the public can use to sit and view the water.  Public parking lot across street.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Stamford Harbor Office Park Waterfront Walkway
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Stamford Harbor Office Park Waterfront Walkway is located behind an office building and offers a nice manicured walkway along the water where one can look out onto a marina.  There is a public access sign posted at the site.

Stroll Stonington Borough's streets lined with exquisite 18th and 19th century homes as part of your visit to the Dodge Paddock and Beal Preserves. Here you can explore the village's quiet corner, including paths wandering through an upland meadow lined with impressive stone walls. Extremely limited on-site parking. Park on off-site streets were allowed to extend your walk.

Stroll this small crescent beach and the adjacent McCook Park trails followed by a dip in the shallow waters at this beach that's perfect for youngsters still learning to swim. Parking passes are available at the Cini Park gate Friday-Sunday and at McCook Point Park lower bath house on other days.  Car-top boat launching restricted to the area immediately west of the groin at the beach.

The St. Ann Club offers a waterfront walkway along the east side of the Norwalk River on the premises of a private boat club that includes a small marina.  It is necessary for visitors to park their vehicles at the state-owned, unimproved parking lot south of and adjacent to the club's property, which is immediately north of the Interstate 95 bridge.  Visitors must access this site as pedestrians traversing the parking lot at St. Ann Club.

Launch your boat (cartop or otherwise) from this beautiful site! Even if you don’t have a boat, there is a nice little viewing area where you can sit to observe the water and the wildlife or enjoy your lunch at the picnic table. This hidden gem of a spot offers direct access to the Connecticut River, as long as you have an access sticker from the town of Chester. If you are not a Chester resident, you must purchase an annual park pass to access this site. The launch is open daily from 6AM-10PM. Swimming is prohibited.

Visitors can enjoy and explore the Connecticut River by launching their car-top boats at Brockway Ferry Landing.  This location is an official stop on the Deep River Canoe and Kayak Guide. Second image below is pathway to River from the road. Look for boulder shown here to find path to the River.

The City Boat Ramp offers a nice vantage point from which to view New Haven Harbor.  Parking May through September at this site is for City residents only. Non-resident car top boaters can launch here but must park on nearby City streets where permitted. No trailer parking on streets.

West Wharf Beach offers a fishing pier with scenic views of Long Island Sound.  The pier (wharf) was once used for ship building in earlier days. This site has a small and quiet beach area and also offers car-top boat access. Memorial Day through Labor Day.  Access is limited to Town resident season pass holders and day pass holders. Day passes are available for purchase by non-residents at the Town's Surf Club Beach facility. See the Madison Town web site for more information. No pets allowed at any time.
Triplett Park is a small grassy field offering views of the waterfront. Limited on street parking is available on Pearl St.
Car top boat launch with  signage.  Visitors should plan launching and returns within 2 hours of scheduled high tide or risk standing in muflats.
Enjoy panoramic views of a healthy salt marsh and Fishers Island Sound at the terminus of a 500 foot path with boardwalk over freshwater wetlands.  Park on grassy area along street opposite of site.

Pull up a bench at Clifton Street Boat Launch, a neighborhood scale coastal access area within the historic Fair Haven section of the City of New Haven and enjoy fine views of the Quinnipiac River. Be careful not to trample the marsh vegetation along the River as this area is being restored.

This car-top only boat launch at the terminus of Knollwood Drive is accessed by turning at the grassy island with a large boulder at intersection with Neptune Drive (see site photo). Waterfront is posted with Town sign marked 'Public Access Right-of-Way.' Water depths at low tide could strand boaters in mud flats. Park off of paved section of road. Obey any posted parking restrictions.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Jordan Cove Water Access is a small barrier beach site.  It is accessed through a densely developed neighborhood with little on-street parking.  Visitors should respect the neighborhood by parking off-street within the site's fenced parking area.  Visitors should avoid trampling the dune grass as they enter the site, and they should also beware of debris on the beach and dune areas.  Visitors crossing the breach to the adjacent island must be aware that a rising tide may strand them on the island (thus, it is best not to cross the breach).  Boaters need to be especially careful when navigating the waters off this site, as abandoned pilings create EXTREMELY HAZARDOUS boating conditions.

The Baker Cove Subdivision Overlook includes a public path from Shennecossett Road to the waterfront at Baker Cove. The site's waterfront offers views of a tidal marsh and its wildlife across the cove. The 2-vehicle "parking lot" is a small roadside pull-off area immediately on your left as you enter the subdivision access road. A gravel access path leads to the overlook area. Follow the grassy area and keep the large white fence to your right to reach the overlook.

Saugatuck Rowing Club has three public access parking spaces and provides beautiful views of the Saugatuck River. Visitors can sit on benches along the waterfront walkway and observe the graceful sport of rowing.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Charles Wheeler Wildlife Management Area offers beautiful views of the Nells Island marshes where visitors may observe a variety of marsh and wading birds. The site accommodates car-top boating access year-round. The gate to the trailered boat launch section of the site however is open only from September 1st until end of February for goose hunting season. The area is not open to trailered (motorized) boats at other times to protect nesting marsh birds. To help you reach Charles Wheeler Wildlife Management Area, some routes leading to this site are posted with boat launch symbol signs.

At Quinnipiac Meadows, enter the main pedestrian path by passing between a chain link gate and a neighbor’s Jersey barrier-based fence. A sign on the entrance gate reminds the visitor that this site is a nature preserve and to enjoy it with respect for resident and migrating wildlife. Extensive tidal wetlands and creeks along the pedestrian path offer glimpses of the water through the site’s dense vegetative cover. Educational signage is provided along the way describing the history of the site itself as well as the preservation efforts currently underway. A popular activity here is the opportunity to walk the meadows observing birds inhabiting one of New Haven’s premier estuarine wildlife areas.

Great overlook of lower Connecticut River with interpretive signage.  There is a short trail out to the old Baldwin Bridge abutment.  The trail begins across the street from the commuter parking lot.  Parking is available in the commuter lot on Route 156.  This site is easily accessed off I-95.

The marina grounds are open to the public although some site amenities (e.g., pool) are reserved for marina patrons.  Exquisite landscaping and views of Norwich Harbor are the hallmark of this boating and coastal facility.  Plenty of benches and shaded rest areas provide comfortable places to linger at this site on a summer day.  An on-site seasonal restaurant offers food and beverages both indoors and out with view of the harbor.

This park, complete with a gazebo to escape the sun, offers excellent fishing opportunities from piers.  This site is a particularly popular fishing area during the fall striped bass season.  Arrange your visit during one of the seasonal summer music programs by contacting the City of Norwich Department of Parks and Cemeteries.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Outstanding example of Thames River estuarine tidal wetland and shoreland forest natural area.  Ten minute walk to pristine shoreline from parking area/access trail.  Parking area and access trail begin just west of Route 2A wetland/tidal creek crossing.  Avoid entering dangerous abandoned incinerator area adjacent to the access trail.  Extensive upland trail system throughout the site's hemlock forest.  Be sure to bring your camera to this site!

A mile long hiking trail leading to a secluded Cove on the Thames River makes this site unique in the highly developed lower Thames River basin.  The Cove's brackish to freshwater marshes provide regionally-signficant fish and wildlife habitat.  Please do not disturb birds nesting or feeding within this near pristine cove.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: Mohegan Tribe of Indians of Connecticut
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: The Shantok-Village of Uncas public access site provides views of the Thames River and picnic areas.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: It looks like a medieval fortress, but a step inside the stone castle reveals the built-in couches, table trackway, and woodcarvings that all point to the creative genius that was William Gillette.  The castle, built in 1919 rests on beautiful grounds that offer picnic tables and hiking trails open to the public without fee.  Fee to enter Castle and receive a guided tour.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This is truly a place to "get away from it all." The island park is accessible by water only. Primitive riverside campsites are available. Check the DEEP State Park website for details. Reservations required.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This site offers car-top boat launch access to the Quinnipiac River and is the closest public launch to the Quinnipiac’s tidal marshes.  Paddlers can navigate both up and downstream the Quinnipiac River from this location during normal river flow conditions.  The site is just south of the Quinnipiac River State Park enabling boaters to paddle up-river to visit this Park. Visitors can also easily access the landward portion of the park which is adjacent to this site.  The boat launch ramp only extends to the high water mark and silty conditions waterward of the ramp can make launching difficult during periods of low water.  Tree  “blow-downs” across the river may create hazardous conditions on this narrow waterway.  Contact the Quinnipiac River Watershed Association (QRWA) for current river conditions prior to launching. QRWA may be contacted at (203) 237-2237, by e-mail at qrwainfo@att.net  or  use their website http://www.qrwa.org/.  It is strongly recommended to limit launching and landing at this site to times of predicted high water to avoid being stranded in mudflats .  Tide tables for this area are available http://www.freetidetables.com/state/Connecticut/sid/21156d98 . Remember to adjust the times in the tide tables to account for the lag in the tides from the tide station at New Haven Harbor to this launch site in North Haven.
Enjoy views of the Thames River from the U.S. Coast Guard Academy.  There are walkways along the Thames River and there is an access pier available at this site.

If you want solitude, you'll find plenty of shade to relax in and view the Thames River from a variety of prominent locations at this site. The park has some playground equipment as well. A footbridge across the railroad that previously provided access to an unimproved area along the River is now closed due to safety concens.

Mystic Seaport Museum, the largest maritime museum in North America, is located on a 40-acre property on the Mystic River.  This historic waterfront museum hosts berthed ships, exhibits, demonstrations of traditional maritime skills, formal classes, activities for children, and overnight dockage for transient vessels.  There is an entrance fee for Mystic Seaport Museum.  More information about the museum can be found on the web at www.mysticseaport.org.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This recently updated boat launching facility provides good access to small boat fishing opportunities for a variety of species. Striped bass, bluefish and flounder fishing spots are all accessible from this location. Plenty of parking is available in the parking lot for trailers. To help you reach Thames River State Boat Launch, some routes leading to this site are posted with boat launch symbol signs.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Located on the Thames River off of Fairview Avenue (underneath the Gold Star Bridge), this property offers large and small boat launching, with trailer parking.  This area is also widely used for recreational fishing.  Public parking provided.  State-owned.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: The 1,013-acre Barn Island Wildlife Management Area is the State's single largest coastal property managed for wildlife conservation. The property provides a diversity of ecosystem and habitats including hilly uplands, agricultural/open fields, mixed hardwood forests and salt, brackish and freshwater tidal wetlands. The site is a popular hiking, wildlife observation and hunting area. *Deer hunting is allowed in-season at this site. Hikers are reminded to exercise caution when using the site during hunting season. Please check the CT DEEP Wildlife Division website for details.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Add a touch of reality to your Revolutionary War history lesson with a visit to Fort Griswold Battlefield State Park, site of the 1781 massacre led by the traitorous Benedict Arnold.  Visitors can learn more about the park by visiting its museum.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This semi-improved coastal access area on the Pawcatuck River provides unique shore-based fishing and car-top boating launching opportunities at the site of a former boat basin. Anglers can fish the former boat basin for Tomcod or fish the deeper waters along the River's shoreline for striped bass. Large boulders adjacent to the shore provide casting platforms for anglers. BE CAREFUL when accessing the rocks, when wet they are extremely slippery. The former boat basin also provides an excellent site for launching small car-top craft--paddle upstream to Pawcatuck River Park just downstream of the Route 1 Bridge or down-stream to the Barn Island Wildlife Management Area. Site visitors may also walk the main trail extending from the parking area to the River. An alternative trail leads from the parking area to the River but is less well defined. Both walkways provide birding opportunities and general passive enjoyment of the River and tidal marshes. The park closes at sunset for all activities other than angling---this policy is strictly enforced. Hunting is not permitted at this park.

The Connecticut River Museum, a National Historic Register site, provides education exhibits and programs describing the past uses and conditions of the Connecticut River. The grounds, including a waterfront access pier, are open to the public without fee and provide an exceptional location to enjoy the River, or to fish.

Located at the southern end of Water Street, this is a working boatyard. Pursuant to a 1992 amendment to the marina's site plan, public use is limited to the pile-supported acess pier. Privately-owned.

Poquonnock River Walkway includes a boardwalk along the east side of the Poquonnock River and parklets at both ends of the walkway.  This site offers picnicking, a play area and several observation points.
Launch a boat at the Peruzzotti Boat Launch or carry in a car-top boat and enjoy paddling in Poquonnock River.  A seasonal food concession is available.  Sanitary facilities are available.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Bluff Point State Park and Reserve
ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Located at the end of Depot Road, this approximately 800 acre State reserve lies between the Poquonnock River and Mumford Cove. One of the largest natural areas in the State, it contains not only a variety of wildlife, but also a barrier beach, steep cliffs, forested lands and tidal wetlands. You can paddle up beyond the railroad bridge to the north and down to Bushy Point Beach. Hiking and running trails offer vistas of Long Island Sound, Mumford Cove and the Pequonnock River.

Turtle Creek Wildlife Sanctuary is a great place to observe wildlife. Take the 1/4 mile 'white dot' hiking trail from the sign that welcomes visitors to the Sanctuary to a sandy beach on the CT River.  Bear rigth at the trail junctions and cross a small wetland/stream to find the the beach hiding behind shoreline vegetation.

Jordan Mill Park provides great wildlife observation and relaxation in the middle of a subdivision. There is a brown and white Long Island Sound public access sign on Great Neck Road pointing to Trumbull Lane. Once on Trumbull Lane look for a roadway that looks like a private drive in-between #15 and #17 Trumbull Lane. Drive down this public access road and you will find parking for 15 cars in a beautiful wooded area. There is a pavilion with picnic tables looking out onto a Jordan Mill Pond, next to a waterfall. On the opposite side there is a car-top boat launch (in addition to trails). To help you reach Jordan Mill Park, some routes leading to this site are posted with the brown and white Long Island Sound Access sign.

A small 'neighborhood beach' near New London harbor. Lifeguards provide supervised swimming seasonally. Food concessions and picnic tables are available. Sanitary facilities are available. There is limited on-street parking with a 2 hour limit. Inquire with lifeguard about longer-term daily parking pass at nearby lot. This is mostly a neighborhood beach that residents walk to (but still open to the public).

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Located off of Brook street in Noank, this approximately 200 acre park is located next to Palmer Cove. Originally a 17th century farm, the property has diverse plant and wildlife communities. Recreational opportunities include bicycling, running, walking and picnicking. There is a small public parking lot at the park’s entrance. State-owned.

This 3.6 acre parcel is located on Palmer Cove in the Tanglewood Subdivision. It contains a children's play area and unimproved car-top boat launch. This open space area offers panoramic views of Palmer Cove. A vehicle turn-around is provided. Limited parking is available. Town-owned.

This waterfront park, located on Beebe Cove off Spicer Avenue, offers picnic facilities and active recreation facilities (volleyball, multi-purpose field, car-top boat launch).  The park is closed at dusk and reservations are necessary for large groups (860-536-5680).  The administrative offices of the Town Parks and Recreation Department are located in the historic Spicer House at this site.  Limited public parking.
East Rock Park with its shady, winding trails provide views of East Rock. Long Island Sound and access to the West River.  A winding road traversing the Park follows the path of the River.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Visitors can launch their car-top or trailered boats at Niantic River State Boat Launch.  Sanitary facilities are available at this site.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Rocky Neck’s varied terrain offers something for everyone. The park has a wide sand beach, a diverse trail system, camping, and saltwater fishing. Visitors have the opportunity of catching mackerel, striped bass, blackfish, and flounder along the stone jetty. Camping requires reservations during the summer. Please note lifeguards are not at all stations.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Enjoy the panoramic views of Long Island Sound from Eolia, the elegant summer mansion of the Harkness family set on over 230 seaside acres of sweeping lawns, with stately trees and spectacular gardens.

Located off of Groton Long Point Road, this park offers a man-made beach area approximately 600 feet long. The park provides facilities for saltwater swimming and picnicking under a grove of shade trees. A snack bar, restrooms and lifeguards are available during the summer season. This site offers views of Long Island Sound and Mouse Island.

Eastern Point Beach is a small family-oriented beach at the mouth of the Thames River near the University of Connecticut's Avery Point campus. The site offer showers, picnic tables, concession stand and playground. Shallow water depths along the beach and seasonal supervised swimming also make this beach a favorite for families. Seasonal parking stickers are available for purchase on an annual basis. A daily parking fee is also an option.

After a swim or walk at this Park's beach, enjoy a picnic lunch or dinner under the large copper beech tree atop a bluff overlooking Long Island Sound. Obtain a day pass at the Park's lower bath house to access this site's diverse recreational opportunties.

Located at the mouth of the Thames River, this 77 acre branch of the University of Connecticut offers sweeping views of Long Island Sound. The campus contains buildings that were once part of a large waterfront estate. This site is best suited for walking and provides views of Fishers Island Sound, New London Ledge Lighthouse and the Thames River.

Waterford Beach Park offers visitors a rare opportunity to experience a largely unmodified Long Island Sound beach, dune and saltmarsh complex. Approximately 1/4 mile of the Park's shoreline provides one of the best examples of an intact beach and dune system in Connecticut where the State-threatened piping plover occasionally nests. Please avoid areas marked as beach nesting bird habitat. Handicapped accessible beach wheelchairs available. Sseason passes are sold through the Parks and Recreation Department. Lifeguards on duty, conditions permitting, during the summer. Follow signs to the adjacent Eugene O'Neil Theater to find this site off of Great Neck Road. Consult the Town of Waterford's website or call the Parks and Recreation Department (860-444-5881) for a current fee schedule.

Ocean Beach Park provides the total beach experience including a rare wide sandy beach, 1/2 mile boardwalk, a water slide, and nature walk with an observation platform in a reclaimed dune area. Other facilities includes an Olympic size outdoor pool, a large pavilion, and new fenced in playscape. Visitors can view the New London Ledge Lighthouse while walking the boardwalk or sandy beach. There is a platform (funded by the LIS license plate fund) for wildlife observation and a nature walk along Alewife Cove. Fee to access site. For more information and to check the current fee schedule see Ocean Beach Park.

West River Memorial Park is a linear park (1.2 miles) that offers 200 acres of undeveloped park land, water and brackish marsh for nature-based outdoor recreation.  The park connects to Edgewood Park and West Rock State Park to the north through a series of pedestrian easements.  These three parks form a nearly continuous, largely undeveloped recreation facility with the West River at its heart.  The car top boat launch at this site is located near the intersection of Marginal Drive and Orange Avenue (Route 1) on the West Haven side of the park.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: CT DEEP Marine Headquarters-Ferry Landing Park
ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Beautiful boardwalk with impressive views of the mouth of the Connecticut River.  Site of several tidal wetland restoration projects.  Nice observation deck at end of boardwalk.  Parking is limited.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Roger Tory Peterson Wildlife Management Area
ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This site, accessible only by canoe or kayak, provides visitors with birding, fishing, and crabbing opportunities within one of Connecticut's largest brackish marshes. Visitors can launch their boats at the nearby Great Island State Boat Launch to access this site. Visitors MUST NOT physically access the marsh, although they may explore the creeks within the marsh in non-motorized vessels. Motorized boats are not allowed within this sensitive marsh that provides critical habitat to waterbirds who feed and breed here. Please observe posted signs regarding osprey nesting.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Visitors can launch their car-top or trailered boats at Dock Road State Boat Launch. This boat launch is adjacent to Pleasure Beach and provides shallow draft vessel access to nearby coves and embayment’s. However, please use extreme caution when navigating the shallow waters of Jordon Cove adjacent to this launch as partially submerged obstructions in this cove can pose boating safety hazards. To help you reach Dock Road State Boat Launch, some routes leading to this site are posted with the brown and white Long Island Sound Access sign.

Quinnipiac River Park is a linear park along the Quinnipiac River.   Benches provided along the river provide a place to rest. The shorefront across the river provides a views of the historic Fair Haven neighborhood.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Seaside State Park,  Connecticut's newest coastal State park, offers limited passive recreational opportunities with few support facilities. CT DEEP is currently evaluating options to redevelop this former tuberculosis sanitarium as an overnight stay destination facility capable of supporting a variety of public outdoor recreation activities. The site's nearly 1/4 mile of sand and cobble beach, historic structures of architectural significance, lawn and fields offer expansive views of Long Island Sound.

In the shadow of the New Haven skyline Criscuolo Park a green jewel of a waterfront park.  This is a multi-use green space with amenities including a playscape, two baseball diamonds, a full basketball court and a paved perimeter for walking.  James Street ends just beyond the park known to be a popular urban fishing spot.

Long Wharf Pier occasionally berths tour boats and visiting tall ships during the summer. The pier is 600 feet long. Check the schedule Schooner Sound Learning for the Schooner Quinnipiac, New Haven's flagship schooner that departs from this site. The pier is a popular birding spot. Time your visit during low tide and you're sure to see a variety of shore and wading birds feeding along Connecticut largest and most productive intertidal mudflat.

Vietnam Veterans Memorial Park is a pleasant green space close to a vibrant urban center with expansive views of New Haven Harbor.  A trail through this property connecting to Long Wharf Park and Long Wharf Nature Preserve make this park a popular area for walking with refreshing cool breezes off the Sound.  The giant black granite “V” commemorates Vietnam veterans.

East Shore Park offers a harbor setting with something for everyone.  The harbor setting is ideal for fishing.  Walkways allow for strolling through the park itself.  The paved asphalt walkways are primarily suited toward visual access of New Haven Harbor, as there is only one access point directly to the harbor.  Bring binoculars and enjoy watching the birds and wildlife.  The park has a playground for children, and it also has park benches.  A seasonal food concession is available, in addition to a limited number of picnic tables.  Sanitary facilities are available.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Stewart B. McKinney National Wildlife Refuge-Salt Meadow Unit
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Stewart B. McKinney National Wildlife Refuge-Salt Meadow Unit provides some beautiful trails for observing birds and wildlife. A tidal river and tidal wetlands can be observed off of one of the trails. This site also boasts some unique architecture in the form of the Enoch Murdock House- its grounds are well-maintained and perfect for some photography or a leisurely stroll. Dogs, cycling and fishing aresome of the uses not allowed at this site. There are designated parking spots for both cars and buses, making this an ideal spot for a school trip!
The entire family can enjoy this coastal site.  Fort Saybrook has educational signs, boardwalks and marshviews.  Parking is free.

Well-worn unimproved trails with many educational placards along the way, Long Wharf Nature Preserve is a secret garden, next to Vietnam Veterans Memorial Park. Power walk and learn about the Sound at the same time. Or, better yet, just meander around the trails and enjoy being this close to the water. Unrestricted views of the harbor, pleasant breezes and the gentle hum of an interstate highway as white noise in the background. Well worth a family visit for its educational value alone. This site is easy to miss, but worth the visit.
The public can stroll along a walkway next to a marina and enjoy viewing the wildlife.  Parking is available at the adjacent Fort Saybrook.

White Sands Beach offers views of Long Island Sound and a picnic area from a gazebo. However, there is NO ON-SITE PARKING for non-residents. It is recommended that nonresidents walk/ride bikes/be dropped off at the beach. See Town of Old Lyme Recreation Department website for more on parking restrictions.
West Beach is the largest of the Westbrook town beaches. In season, sanitary facilities and a food concession are available. Non-resident day use parking pass may be obtained at the beach gate.

Surf Club is a Town-owned 45-acre park on Long Island Sound with picnic areas, sports facilities, and supervised beach swimming. Coast Guard approved life vests are permitted but rafts or other inflatables are prohibited. Seasonal food concessions and restrooms operate Memorial Day through Labor Day. Access to the Park during the summer season is available by purchasing a season pass available at the Madison Recreation Office Mon.-Fri. 8:30-4pm, by mail or by purchasing a day use pass. Consult the trail map to access the Park's Garvan trail which begins from the road leading to the boat racks. Pets not allowed during the summer beach season. All other times pets must be kept on leash and only allowed in parking lots or nature trails (no pets allowed on beach or in picnic area).

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Hammonasset Beach State Park is Connecticut's largest shoreline park and beach hosting over 2 miles of sandy beach and 3/4 miles of boardwalk. To access the Park's car-top boat launch, follow signs to  Meigs Point and the fishermen's parking area. The launch is on east side of Meigs Point jetty.
This small, shallow-water beach has a bathhouse with showers on-site.  Visitors should contact the Old Saybrook Parks & Recreation Department at (860) 395-3152 for up-to-date fee schedules.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Great Harbor Wildlife Management Area offers a small sandy beach at low tide and views of tidal marsh of Joshua Cove and Long Island Sound. Limited parking is available in the turn-around at the end of Trolley Road. Exercise extreme caution when approaching the breachway through the rip-rap at the mouth of the Cove as strong tidal currents here create potentially hazardous conditions. Do not attempt to navigate the breachway during periods of strong currents. If paddling Long Island Sound from this site, use the Trolley Road Coastal Access Site beach 200 feet to the east to land your canoe/kayak if upon your return currents through the breachway are treacherous.

Chittenden Park features a scenic boardwalk to Long Island Sound, where you can relax at a fantastic viewing area overlooking the water. This site also has sports fields, picnic tables and even a few bocce courts. This is the Southernmost point of the New England Trail, running from here all the way through Connecticut and Massachusetts to the New Hampshire border.

Located at the mouth of the East River, the Guilford Town Marina provides boat access to Guilford Harbor and Long Island Sound with scenic views of Faulkners Island. Contact town dockmaster at 203-453-8092 for current fee schedule.

Fort Nathan Hale Park offers on New Haven Harbor offers a sandy beach and a variety of other amenities.  Fishing from the access pier is expected to resume late 2017 upon its reconstruction. Bring binoculars for birding, and walk the site's trails.  Interpretive signage along the trails educates visitors about on-site habitat and the property's historic and cultural values .  A pavilion provides shade from the summer sun.  A family friendly playground is available on this site.  Sanitary facilities are available.
Sandy Point is a long stretch of sandy beach extending into New Haven Harbor that is popular for birding.

East Wharf Beach is a town beach with a fishing pier once used as a ship building location in earlier days. Shellfishing is available west of the pier only. A gazebo offers scenic views of Long Island Sound. Memorial Day through Labor Day access is limited to pass holders .  Access is limited to Town resident season pass holders and day pass holders. Day passes are available for purchase by non-residents at the Town's Surf Club Beach facility. See the Madison Town web site for more information. No pets allowed at any time.

Jacob’s Beach is a small sandy beach with with a playscape, picnic tables, and a beach volleyball court. Swimming is best at high tide. This site has car-top boat access, and racks for kayak storage are available for rent on-site adjacent to the car-top boat access area, with approximately a total of 100 spaces available. Handicapped accessibility to kayak and canoe launch area is available.

Clinton Town Marina is located in Clinton Harbor and is adjacent to the Clinton Town Marina Boat Launch.  This area is ideal for watching boats in Clinton Harbor while strolling a boardwalk.  Benches and picnic tables facing the Harbor are easily accessible from the nearby parking lot.

Painter Park provides primarily developed recreational facility including picnic areas, tennis courts, ball fields, a playground and the City's recreation office.  Tidal wetlands along the Cove River at this site provide the only coastal experience at this highly developed Park.  Birders may wish to visit the site to view marsh birds.

Clinton Town Beach is a sandy beach facing the entrance to Clinton Harbor with views of Long Island Sound.  The site provides  a car-top boat launch area, a walkway leading to an old stone bridge that crosses the Hammock River at the entrance. In season, sanitary facilities and a food concession are open to the public. A pavilion is available for picnic lunches as well as a viewing platform with interpretive signs to enjoy wildlife in adjacent tidal marshes. Non-residents require a daily parking pass, which is available at the beach from 9AM to 3PM. Refer to the site's website for current fee schedule.
This municipal park suitable for passive recreational use with few facilities. Site offers views of the mouth of the West River, Long Island Sound and Faulkner’s Island.

Sandy Point Bird Sanctuary is a great place for bird watching. The site is sometimes closed during the beach nesting breeding season. There is a parking lot on-site. West Haven provides 3.5 miles of public beach or Waterfront Park, each with its own amenities or environmental setting. Most are connected through a 1.7 mile walkway providing pedestrians, bicyclists and roller-bladers a continuous waterfront urban “greenway.” Views of Long Island Sound exist throughout most of the walkway. Most beach parking lots in West Haven close at 11:30 p.m. although the walkway is open 24 hours, every day.

Morse Beach is a large sandy beach. Visitors can enjoy distant views of the lighthouse in New Haven Harbor. A rocky outcropping into the Long Island Sound is suitable for fishing. Two benches are available for resting. West Haven provides 3.5 miles of public beach or Waterfront Park, each with its own amenities or environmental setting. Beaches from Bradley Point Park to Sandy Point are networked through a 1.7 mile walkway providing pedestrians, bicyclists and roller-bladers a continuous waterfront urban “greenway.” Views of Long Island Sound exist throughout most of the walkway. Most beach parking lots in West Haven close at 11:30 p.m. although the walkway is open 24 hours, every day. Some routes leading to this site are posted with the brown and white Long Island Sound Access sign.

Pardee Park is a narrow linear park providing wonderfull views of Morris Cove and a concrete walkway for stolling in the neigbhorhood scale along New Haven Harbor. Trail connections  to Fort Nathan Hale Park to the north provide for a longer waterfront walk.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This 62-acre State Park can accessed from Short Beach Road, where trails lead to the waterfront portion of the Park. The site provides outstanding views of the Farm River and excellent birding opportunities. The Park’s waterfront is accessed by foot from a small public parking area adjacent to an electrically-controlled gate at the site's access road off Mansfield Grove Road. The Park is closed at sunset to the general public and dogs must be on leash. Quinnipiac University has terminated their contract to manage the marina at the park.  DEEP is working on a plan to manage the site.

Peck Beach is a narrow beach nearly a mile long.  Two stairways cross over sandy dunes to access sandy beach and waterfront.  Parking is available at a City parking lot at Morse Beach about 3/4 miles to the east of Peck Beach.  Visitors are advised to drop off beach gear with a companion at Peck Beach before parking and walking to this beach.  No on-street parking allowed.  West Haven provides 3.5 miles of public beach or waterfront park, each with its own amenities or environmental setting.  Beaches from Bradley Point Park to Sandy Point are networked through a 1.7 mile walkway providing pedestrians, bicyclists and roller-bladers a continuous waterfront urban “greenway.” Views of Long Island Sound exist throughout most of the walkway.  Most beach parking lots in West Haven close at 11:30 p.m. although the walkway is open 24 hours, every day.

Alschuler Beach is accessible from an extensive boardwalk. Beach parking is available at the Savin Rock Conference Center when it is not in use. West Haven provides 3.5 miles of public beach or Waterfront Park, each with its own amenities or environmental setting. Beaches from Bradley Point Park to Sandy Point are networked through a 1.7 mile walkway providing pedestrians, bicyclists and roller-bladers a continuous waterfront urban “greenway.” Views of Long Island Sound exist throughout most of the walkway. Most beach parking lots in West Haven close at 11:30 p.m. although the walkway is open 24 hours, every day.

Oak Street Beach is a sandy beach with a pier. This site is ideal for fishing. Night lights installed on the pier make walking out on the pier for strolling or fishing more pleasant. This beach is the site of recorded music four nights a week during the summer season. West Haven provides 3.5 miles of public beach or Waterfront Park, each with its own amenities or environmental setting. Beaches from Bradley Point Park to Sandy Point are networked through a 1.7 mile walkway providing pedestrians, bicyclists and roller-bladers a continuous waterfront urban “greenway.” Views of Long Island Sound exist throughout most of the walkway. Oak Street Beach Activity Building is a multi-use activity building adjacent to Oak Street Beach. Most beach parking lots in West Haven close at 11:30 p.m. although the walkway is open 24 hours, every day. Some routes leading to this site are posted with the brown and white Long Island Sound Access sign.

Bradley Point Park includes a small sandy beach and a developed walkway parallel to Long Island Sound. Park benches on-site provide vantage points for visitors to enjoy extensive views. Three sets of permanent posts for impromptu volleyball games are available on the sandy beach (in-season), thereby broadening the number of possible recreational opportunities for visitors. A temporary portable toilet serves as the only restroom facility on-site. A spectacular 4th of July fireworks display occurs annually. On-site parking is available for 40 vehicles; contact the West Haven Parks & Recreation Department for parking fee schedule (effective from Memorial Day Weekend through Labor Day Weekend annually). Most beach-parking lots in West Haven close at 11:30 p.m. on a daily basis, although the walkway is open 24 hours per day, year-round.

Lighthouse Point Park offers something for everyone.  One can view the 70-foot tall Five-Mile Point Lighthouse constructed in the 1840’s and also the Southwest Ledge Light, a scenic operating lighthouse.  Both car-top and trailered boat access to Long Island Sound.  A boat ramp provides saltwater winter boaters with access to New Haven Harbor, but strong northwesterly winter winds make the return trip back to shore tricky.  The Park offers canoes and kayaks more protected access to coastal waters at a sandy area near the mouth of Morris Creek, located at the east end of the Park’s beach past the bathhouses.   Stop by the large blue and white pavilion near the lighthouse to see the restored historic carousel (operates summer only).  Visit the rangers during warm weather when they offer sea-kayak rental and instruction.  For up-to-date information, visit the New Haven Parks and Recreation website.

Seabluff Beach, adjacent to Bradley Point Park, is one of West Haven's largest beaches (parking fee applies). Three sets of volleyball posts are installed here for public use. This beach marks the western end of the West Haven beaches walkway. A linear parking lot and temporary sanitary facilities are in place at this site. West Haven provides 3.5 miles of public beach or waterfront park, each with its own amenities or environmental setting. Most are networked through a 1.5 mile walkway providing pedestrians, bicyclists and roller-bladers a continuous waterfront urban greenway experience. Views of Long Island Sound exist throughout most of the walkway. Most beach parking lots in West Haven close at 11:30 p.m. although the walkway is open 24 hours, every day.

Dawson Avenue Beach is a wide sandy beach with some shallow water areas provides an ideal place for a family picnic with small children.  The adjoining Abbot Park on Ocean Avenue provides a lawn area with benches for those who prefer to enjoy views of Long Island Sound well removed from the beach.

East Haven Town Beach is a sandy beach with a picnic area, bocci ball and beach volleyball courts. There are also showers and pavilion available at this site. Parking in town lots is only available to East Haven Residents with a parking pass. Non-residents are only allowed to use limited free on-street parking to access this beach. No beach fee.

South Street Beach offers visitors a sandy crescent beach and grassy area to enjoy Long Island Sound.  This beach is the furthest removed from the City of West Haven strand of beaches to the east.  Rocky outcroppings at this site provide good fishing spots.  South Street Beach is well-suited for those looking for a quieter beach experience.  Parking lot accessibility is best one block north of South Street, directly across from Linwood Street.

Wilcox Park features an extensive trail system through a forest adjacent to Milford Harbor.  The trails lead to a cantilevered wooden platform that offers excellent views of Milford harbor and the wide variety of boating activity it supports.  The site also hosts a boat ramp with parking for vehicles and trailers.  Boaters must obtain a parking pass to access the launch.  See the Milford Harbor Commission section of the City's website for details on boating access facilities or call 203-874-1610 for a fee schedule.

Gulf Beach is a beautiful sandy beach with an access pier for fishing, picnic areas, and restrooms. Visitors have a view of Charles Island. There is a parking lot for residents on-site and non-resident parking is located across the street (fee charged).

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Silver Sands State Park features a 3/4 mile boardwalk connecting the State park to the City of Milford's Walnut Beach Park. The site includes an offshore island connected to the mainland by a sand and gravel bar (tombolo) that is submerged at high tide. Accessing the tombolo is EXTREMELY DANGEROUS and should be avoided. Access to the island is prohibited May 1 through August 31 to protect heron and egret rookeries. To help you reach Silver Sands State Park, some routes leading to this site are posted with boat launch symbol signs. Access to the Park in the evening is available to marine anglers only via the small parking area at the end of East Broadway located at the south central end of the Park. See the Park map for the location of the marine angler satellite parking area. To help you reach Silver Sands State Park, some routes leading to this site are posted with the brown and white Long Island Sound Access sign.
