ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Visitors can launch either a trailered or cartop boat at Housatonic River State Boat Launch. There is an access pier available at this site for fishing. To help you reach Housatonic River State Boat Launch, some routes leading to this site are posted with boat launch symbol signs. Please observe signage and notice board to ensure that you are conducting only allowable activities and doing so in designated areas. Boat launch is intended ONLY for boat launching and fishing. Dogs are allowed but must be leashed.Parking for waterfowl hunting is available at this site, but hunting must only occur where permitted.

Walnut Beach is a great place to spend the day strolling along the edge of the Long Island Sound or fishing from the pier. Visitors have a view of Charles Island from this site. The site provides ample parking. Non-Residents visiting Walnut Beach must park in Lot #4 located in the rear of the main parking lot (fees apply).

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: The Connecticut Audubon Coastal Center is an environmental education facility specializing in coastal outdoor education. An elevated observation platform provides visitors with outstanding views of the adjacent Nells Island marsh. A boardwalk across a dune to second observation platform on the beach offer visitors spectacular views of the Sound and expansive intertidal flats where shorebirds often feed. Fees are charged only to enter visitors center. The general public is welcome stroll the Center's grounds for free.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Stewart B. McKinney National Wildlife Refuge-Milford Point Unit
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Stewart B. McKinney National Wildlife Refuge-Milford Point Unit is adjacent to Charles Wheeler Wildlife Management Area.  This site offers views of the Long Island Sound and a chance to view wildlife from an observation platform.  Park at Connecticut Audubon Coastal Center  lot and walk to the beach to site's observation platform (the upland portion of the refuge is closed to public access).  Beach area is open from September 1 to March 31.  No public access to beach at other times.
Seaside Park is an extensive municipal park with many amenities including a bathing beach, bath houses, ball fields, picnic areas, and hiking trails.
Short Beach Park is a large park with many amenities including a par-3 golf course, miniature golf, platform tennis, basketball courts, beach volleyball, playscape, swimming and passive recreation.
Captain’s Cove offers unique maritime tourist experience including waterfront shops, public wharf, and historic attractions. The site provides views of the busy Black Rock Harbor.
Perry's Mill Ponds is a large site with beautiful scenic trails.  Launch your canoe and observe the wildlife along the Mill River.

Nestled between Long Island Sound and the Great Meadows tidal marsh it shelters, Long Beach, at a little over 1 mile in length, is one of the longest barrier beaches in Connecticut. A stroll along the beach surrounds the visitor with dunes, the Great Meadows Marsh and the open waters of the Sound. Many species of shorebirds and waterfowl can be found here, including the 'threatened' Piping plover that nests throughout the summer on the western part of this beach near Pleasure Beach. These birds nest both on the beach and the sandy 'trail' behind the dunes. Therefore, if you must pass areas of nesting birds, please respect the restricted access area signs and pass within or below the wet sand area of the beach to avoid disturbing this rare and beautiful bird. Fishing is permitted outside designated swimming areas. If you intend to visit during hunting season, proper precautions should be taken as hunting is allowed in the Great Meadows Marsh. To help you reach Long Beach, some routes leading to this site are posted with the brown and white Long Island Sound Access sign.
Scenic and sandy neighborhood beach with views of the Fayerweather Island Lighthouse.

The name 'Russian Beach,' (also known locally as Lordship Beach) is derived from its historic use by Russian immigrants employed at Igor Sikorsky's Sikorsky Manufacturing Company, now part of United Technology Corporation's Sikorsky Aircraft. At Russian Beach, only the area waterward of mean high water is open to the public. Walk along the wet sand area of this beach via access provided by the beach at Point-No-Point. Russian Beach is believed to be one of the few natural beaches in Connecticut that is expanding in a seaward direction resulting in a series of dunes.

Boat launch access is available directly after the entrance to Ash Creek Open Space.  Fee charged to access boat ramp at  marina portion of site. No fee for car-top launching.  Non-residents of Town of Fairfield should contact the Town of Fairfield's Marina office (203-256-3010)  for information on obtaining a pass to use the launch ramp for launching trailered-vessels.

There are numerous activities for outdoor enthusiasts to enjoy at Saint Mary’s by the Sea.  A developed walkway (approximately 1/2 mile in length) provides visitors with spectacular views of Long Island Sound and Black Rock Harbor. The site holds historic and cultural interest for visitors to explore. Please contact the Bridgeport Parks & Recreation Department for obtaining a parking permit to visit this site.

Jennings Beach offers visitors a large sandy beach with great views of Long Island Sound.  Also located nearby is Ash Creek Open Space for those visitors who are interested in launching their boats. Visit the Town of Fairfield's Marina web page for more information on boat launching.
This site is a wonderful playground located the near the parking lot for Jennings Beach.

Levitt Pavilion/Westport Riverwalk contains a formal walkway adjacent to the town library that connects to an informal on-grade trail that runs along the Levitt Pavilion waterfront.  The formal walkway contains benches and small shade trees and offers great views across the Saugatuck River.  The informal trail does not meet ADA standards.
Rickards Beach is a sandy beach adjacent next to Penfield Beach. Parking is available at Penfield Beach.
Penfield Beach is a great place to swim and sun along Long Island Sound. It offers a long stretch of sandy beach, swing sets, charcoal grills and a pavilion with a food concession.

Penfield Reef is a small parcel that provides public access to a jetty through a sandy beach for limited passive recreational opportunities, and is accessed via an easement through a private driveway. Visitors can fish and observe wildlife at Penfield Reef. Since there is no parking on-site, visitors should park at nearby Veterans Park on Reef Road. From Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day, a parking permit is required to park at Veterans Park and visitors will need to find on-street parking or park at an alternative public lot.
Pine Creek Recreation Park is a great site for wildlife observation.  Walk along the trails next to the marsh and watch for egrets and herons.  Ample parking.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Have a leisurely lunch in the shade of the picnic grove, swim in Long Island sound, or view marsh life from the observation platform at Sherwood Island State Park. To access the Park's car-top boact launch, follow signs to the east side of East beach to the southeast corner of the parking area beyond the nature center.

Burying Hill Beach and Wetlands is located across the street from Greens Farms Academy, walking distance to Greens Farms railroad station and adjacent to Sherwood Island State Park beach. A small quiet beachfront overlooking Long Island Sound with picnic tables and grills. A parking fee is required from May 1st to September 30th.

Longshore Club Park is located at the mouth of the Saugatuck River. Fishing and limited car-top boating access allowed at marina. Day sailing and kayak rentals and instruction are available at the site's Long Shore Sailing School. Trails and walkways throughout the Park accommodate passive recreational opportunities such as bird watching. A pavilion provides shelter from the sun. Visitors can bring their own lunch and eat at the picnic area or use a seasonal on-site concession stand. A bathhouse with sanitary facilities are provided. A fee is charged to visit the beach at this Park. Car-top boat launching is allowed at the site for non- residents from October to April only. See the Town of Westport website.

Compo Beach and Marina is a 29-acre park with something for everyone. The park features beaches, a concession stand and, pavilion, bath houses with lockers, and picnic areas including grills on south beach. For the more active, the park offers a large playscape, basketball courts, sand volleyball courts, open skate areas, and a softball field. Use of the marina and boat launch area requires a permit. There is a daily fee for non-residents to access the park, although a limited number of beach passes are issued daily. See the 'Site Website' link or contact the Town's Park and Recreation Department at 203-341-5090 for a current fee schedule.

Trails and walkways make it easy to exlplore the of this property's shoreline on an inlet of the Saugatuck River. Bring your binoculars and a birding guide to enjoy the site's natural beauty. Fishing is also permitted at this site.  Compo Colonial Cemetery has historic and cultural interest. On-street parking is available on Compo Beach Rd after Owenoke Park.

Veteran's Memorial State Park and Marina is situated on 35 acres, and includes a marina and boat launch site, a playground, ball fields, bicycle and jogging paths overlooking scenic Norwalk Harbor. Visitor docks with full power available, a boating center and marina. Please call the marina (203-829-8892) for a fee schedule and availability before visiting or visit the Norwalk Visitors' Dock Web page at http://ct-norwalk.civicplus.com/index.aspx?nid=306

North Water Street Park is a small park beside the Sheffield Ferry terminal along the Harbor Loop Trail. It's an excellent spot to watch the harbor's activity from and has many shops and restaurants nearby.
Mill Pond Park is a small park located on the edge of a tidal pond with picnic tables, benches and interpretive signs.
Cockenoe Island is off Seymour Point in Westport and only accessible by boat.  There is a boat launch ramp at Compo Beach and Marina and Saugatuck River State Boat Launch in Westport.

Visitors to Calf Pasture Beach  may  park at the beach upon paying a day use fee.  A café and food concession is available on site. For more parking information visit http://www.norwalkct.org/Facilities/Facility/Details/3

The coastline of Grassy Island is mostly gravel and fine sand and provides sheltered landing areas.  Overnight camping is allowed by a permit from the City of Norwalk. For more information on visting Norwalk's islands, visit http://www.norwalkct.org/580/Island-Parks-Information

The Norwalk Land Trust's Farm Creek Preserve offers trails and an access pier from which visitors can enjoy views of the Farm Creek and Wilson Cove. The Preserve's 16 acres includes four separately acquired parcels hosting tidal marsh, woodland and grassland meadows.  Open dawn to dusk.

Shea Island's shoreline is strewn with rocks and boulders.  Overnight camping is allowed with a permit. For more information on visting Norwalk's islands, visit http://www.norwalkct.org/580/Island-Parks-Information

Cove Island Park has it all, including developed recreation facilities such as a 1-mile loop walking/running trail, children’s play area, a roller blade/cycling path and expansive lawn areas for kite-flying. There are two sandy beaches, a small salt marsh, intertidal mudflats and the estuarine embayment of Holly Pond and the Cove River that provide opportunities for birders to observe water birds. Rocky shoreline areas offer a place for anglers to hook that big one and a small bluff offers an excellent viewpoint for those looking for a place view the Sound while strolling along this first-rate shoreline park. A state-of-the art nature center with displays on Long Island Sound can also be found at the Park. Be sure to consult City's website listed below for required passes/fees to enter park. Non-resident daily and seasonal passes to the Park can now be purchased at the park gate from 10 am to 6 pm daily. Passes can also be purchased at the cashier's office in the Stamford Government Center building, 888 Washington Boulevard, Stamford. For those wishing to visit the site by bus, CT Transit stops at this Park.

Altthough the central feature at this 22-acre park is a beautiful sandy beach, the site also includes picnic areas, a bathhouse, concession stand, children's play areas, 6 tennis courts, 5 paddle tennis courts, and a windsurfing area.  Day passes to enter the Park may be purchased at the Park gate.

Pear Tree Point Beach is an 8-acre beach loaded with amenities picnic tables and grills, a bath house, a gazebo, food concession and boat launch ramp.   Day passess to enter the Park may be purchased at the Park gate.

Cummings Park is a beautiful, 79-acre park on Long Island Sound.  Visitors can enjoy the beach, pavilions, snack bar, board walk and  fishing pier.  The park offers a variety of outdoor recreation facilities including tennis courts, handball and basketball courts, playground, four softball fields, rest rooms and parking.  Consult the City's website listed below for required passes/fees to enter the park. Passes can now be purchased at the park.

Enjoy a picnic by the water in Czescik Marina Park's serene gardens, gazebo and boardwalk. The park extends across Harbor Drive where the hills offer a stunning views of the boats below. Marina parking permits are required for the small lot in front of the marina. They are not required for the larger lot between Harbor Drive and Shippon Avenue.

Kosciuszko Park is a 7-acre waterfront peninsula park that contains a wide walkway around the perimeter, which encircles ball fields and a children's playground. Narrower loop trails extend down closer to the water. The site has plenty of parking and does not require a fee or sticker to access. There is a sign marking the entrance to Kosciuszko Park.

John J. Bocuzzi Park is a coastal park featuring a beach, shady picnic area, sports fields, playground and tennis courts. SoundWaters, an environmental education organization, runs youth sailing and paddling programs here. They also offer kayak and paddleboard rentals 10am-6pm on weekends between Memorial Day and Labor Day.

Greenwich Point Park is a beautiful site offering a large sandy beach and walking trails. Picnic tables are available and they are strategically placed for a great view of the water. There are no public access signs leading to this site. This site has two seasonal shellfishing areas that close during the summer and one approved area on the south side that is open during the summer. Please visit the Town of Greenwich website for information on obtaining a non-resident single entry park pass and parking pass, issued off-site only Monday-Friday (9 am - 6 pm) at the Eastern Greenwich (203) 637-4583 or Budheim Western Greenwich (203) 532-1259 Civic Centers.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Housatonic River Water Access at Great River Golf
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Housatonic River Water Access at Great River Golf provides a pleasant one-quarter mile walkway along 3 holes of golf course on a shaded woodchip path leads to a wooden boardwalk at the River's edge.  A separate footpath runs several hundred feet to the south along the river.

Small salt marsh overlook with parking for two cars. A 50 foot gravel walkway defines the public access area. Parking area is on right 0.30 miles from a railroad crossing on Latimer Point Road past the "Private Road" sign. Public access also includes an elevated wooden walkway/pier at northern end of Noank Shipyard site adjacent at the waterward terminus of Washington Street.

Spencer's Creek Preserve is a small site with a variety of natural habitats.  Walk through uplands and an open meadow near the wetlands along Spencer Creek.  Park at Cox School .25 miles north of the site.  Trail to wetlands is not always easy to follow and visitors may need to exercise caution when exploring this site, especially at high tide when high water may impeded access to marsh.

Guilford Salt Meadows Sanctuary offers a pleasant trail along the upland boundary of a tidal river with substantial tidal wetland fringe.  There is parking available in field past house #5.  Please check the Guilford Salt Meadows Sanctuary website at guilford.audubon.org

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Climb to the top of the fort and witness the most spectacular views of New London harbor, downtown New London, and Fort Griswold across the River in Groton.  Watch the ferries, pleasure boats and Coast Guard patrol boats pass.  Maybe you'll see a submarine!

TGM Anchor Point condominiums and marina provides an excellent fishing pier and extensive walkways providing excellent views of Southfield Harbor. This coastal access facility is adjacent to the condominiums on Southfield Avenue. Designated parking spaces are provided for the public to access this site.

Benches are provided at this pump station located on Gravel Street adjacent to the Mystic River.  This area offers views of the Mystic River drawbridge and Mystic Seaport.  Public parking available.  Town-owned.

This boardwalk fronting the S&P Oyster House restaurant and condominiums is accessed by crossing the restaurant's landscaped area on Main Street near the Mystic River drawbridge. Don't let the sign indicating "private dock" on the walkway dissuade you from accessing the walkway and enjoying fine views of the River during daylight hours.

Mystic River Park is located on the river adjacent to the historic Mystic drawbridge. There is no fee to enter or use the park. Facilities include a waterfront access pier with sitting and fishing areas and dinghy dock for small boats and public restroom. Boaters can access the site for short stays by securing dinghies on-site (no overnight stays allowed) after consulting the dockmaster.

Located off of Water Street, between Steamboat Wharf and Powerhouse Condominiums, this site offers public access behind the Art Association building along the Mystic River.  There is no fee for parking in the lot.  Privately-owned.

A gravel path along the Mystic River winds its way from Water Street past Randall's Wharf Condominiums to the Powerhouse Condominiums. Benches are provided. As this path is associated with Randall’s Wharf Condominiums, consideration of the rights and privacy of the residents is requested. The path is privately-owned, but an easement allows the public to enjoy the views of a marina and the Mystic River. Parking is available, for a fee, north of the site at the Mystic Arts Center parking lot.

A stone/dust path extends from Water Street to a bench area adjacent to the Mystic River, providing scenic views of marinas and the river itself in historic Mystic. Access is confined exclusively to the path. All other areas of the site are privately-owned and not open to the public.

Nott Lane Open Space is a very small point of access to the water at the end of Nott Lane in Essex.  At Nott Lane Open Space visitors can launch car-top boats and paddle along the river.  Bring binoculars and watch birds and wildlife at this site.  Fishing and crabbing are permitted.  It is adjacent to Essex Town Park.

Access the Connecticut River at Alt Water Access Area using a car-top boat and enjoy this historic area.  Visitors can go fishing or crabbing at this site.  Bring binoculars and watch the birds and wildlife at this site.

Novelty Lane Water Access Area is a very small point of access to the Connecticut River at the end of Novelty Lane in Essex, and includes a bench that overlooks the river.  This site is difficult to locate. Look for a brown and white shoreline public access sign at the beginning of a path located on the right before the entrance to the Essex Yacht Club and before a house at the end of Novelty Lane.

This narrow water access at the terminus of Mack Lane offers fishing, car-top boat access and bird watching opportunities. Use caution walking down the hill to access this water. Very limited street parking.
One can enjoy exceptional views of the Connecticut River and Long Island Sound from this site.

At Long Wharf Maritime Center Esplanade, there are plenty of benches for a place to rest after hiking the adjacent Long Wharf and Vietnam Veterans Memorial Parks.  The Esplanade also provides an ideal venue for observing ships visiting New Haven Harbor.  There is a hard surfaced walkway ideal for wheelchairs and strollers.  Not well-signed for public access from Long Wharf Drive.  Access can be gained between the Rusty Scupper and the Maritime Center.  Parking is limited.

The Branford Trolley Trail is a 480 foot long by 4 foot wide footbridge along the path of an abandoned historic trolley track.  The bridge connects to a popular existing nature walk.  Visitors to the Branford trolley track footbridge can expect to see numerous shorebirds in the tidal estuary, feeding in the marsh or wading in the shallow waters of the tidal creek.  This marsh area also provides habitat for many fish, mammals and invertebrates.

This 1.7 mile recreation path along the West Haven beaches provides runners, cyclists, rollerbladers and others with fine views and offshore breezes of Long Island Sound. Park at either terminus of the path at Sandy Point or Bradely Point Park to enjoy the entire length of this recreation path.

Parker Harding Plaza is located in downtown Westport. The waterfront walkway and wooden boardwalk, which extend onto a peninsula, offer great views of the Saugatuck River and associated wetlands.  The site is convenient to shopping and other waterfront public access sites.  Parker Harding Plaza is located adjacent to the Gorham Island public access site. To help you reach Parker Harding Plaza, some routes leading to this site are posted with the brown and white Long Island Sound Access sign.
Daskams Lane Park is a small park along the upper reaches of the Norwalk Harbor.
Village at Stamford Landing provides a nice walkway through a harbor setting.  Visitors can fish or simply enjoy the views of the water.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Stewart B. McKinney National Wildlife Refuge-Great Meadows Unit
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Follow the path that parallels the abandoned railroad tracks to two viewing platforms that provide commanding views of the west side of the marsh. The second (eastern most) platform has a a telescope to view marsh birds.

This site offers access along the docks at Steamboat Wharf from Route 1 to the adjacent Mystic Art Association property through the Water Street public parking area. Benches are provided and parking is also available (parking fee charged during some hours). The elevated piers over the water providing access are associated with the Steamboat Wharf Condominiums. Please respect the privacy of the condominium residents when using this facility. Privately-owned.

This Riverfront trail along the Yantic River and Norwich Harbor includes historic and interpretive signs describing Chelsea, the birthplace of Norwich. The trail follows City streets for short segments. Walk upstream starting from Howard T. Brown Park on Norwich Harbor at Chelsea Harbor Drive to Yantic Falls. To help you reach Heritage Riverfront Park Walkway entrance at Howard T. Brown Park, some routes leading to this site are posted with the brown and white Long Island Sound Access sign .

See and read about the restoration of Bentley Creek Marsh and the wildlife inhabiting this urban salt marsh as well as the history of the redevelopment of the Pfizer site. The site contains the only remaining tidal wetland on the Thames River in New London. On-site interpretive signs provide an inspiring story of the site's transformation from degraded industrial site to a thriving tidal marsh. The site is split into two distinct paths -- one on the north side of the facility, and the other on the south side of the complex. Please refrain from taking photographs, as security personnel at the Pfizer Global Development Facility may become alarmed and question one's motives.

Brewery Square Walkway is a shady, pleasant tree-lined walkway along the River.  There is plenty of lighting for moonlit strolls.  Good improved trail surface for wheelchairs and strollers.  Ferry Street Bridge currently under construction limits on-street parking nearby and some routes to this site.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This is a great location to put in your canoe and experience the Connecticut River.  There is one tent camping site for those traveling down river looking for an overnight stop. Please check the State Parks page www.ct.gov/deep/stateparks page for  for additional information on river camping availability and fees (tent camping for canoeists only limited to one night).

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Branford River Gateway Marsh Viewing Area
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Branford River Gateway Marsh Viewing Area provides wonderful views of the Branford River from an elevated viewing platform.  Plenty of parking available.  Fishing access provided across the street.

Branford Point lookout allows for a nearly 360 degree view of Branford Harbor. Views vary from marinas and recreational boaters using the harbor to the Town Beach. Parking is free, but limited. Fishing is permitted from the stone lookout but the adjacent public dock provides more area to fish from.
A gazebo at Waylands Wharf is available for enjoying scenic views of Stonington Harbor.  The wharf is a short walk from the shopping area in Stonington Borough.

Baybrook Beach is a small sandy beach.  There is a small parking lot which accommodates only 2 or 3 cars.  This site is ideal for bird watching.  Visitors can enjoy a picnic at one of the tables provided.
Kiddie Beach is a small beach on an inlet of the Niantic River provide car-top boat access to the River.  Limited on street parking is available for 4 vehicles.

At the Hammock Point Condominium's access site, a short walk along a path past a gazebo leads visitors to a viewing platform overlooking a scenic tidal marsh along the Patchogue River. Access available from dawn to dusk. Please respect property residents and park in designated spots.

Harbor Point is a walkable, mixed-use development still under construction. The long walkway along the harbor, as well as several shops and restaurants, are already open. The waterfront offers a fishing pier, marinas and water taxi to Harbor Landing.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Stewart B. McKinney National Wildlife Refuge-Sheffield Island Unit
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: The Sheffield Island Unit is a 67-acre island owned by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service with the potential to support nesting wading birds.  A portion of the island is also owned by the Norwalk Seaport Association which maintains a historic lighthouse and facilitates tours.  The Seaport Association and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service cooperatively built a nature trail with observation deck.  Gulls nest along the rocky shoreline in the summer and surrounding waters provide habitat for wintering waterfowl.  The Sheffield Island Lighthouse is maintained and operated seasonally as a museum by the Norwalk Seaport Association.  Public ferry at Hope Dock, 7 Water Street (May-Sept), call 203-838-9744 for info.  The Norwalk Seaport Association provides transportation during the summer from the Maritime Aquarium to Sheffield Island for a fee.  For more information regarding this site including fees, please visit the Norwalk Seaport Association website at www.seaport.org.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Stewart B. McKinney National Wildlife Refuge-Outer Island
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: An 'open' flag on-site is visibly displayed during the times in which the public has permission to access the island. If that particular flag is not displayed, then the public is prohibited from accessing the island (unless they obtain a permit from the US Fish and Wildlife Service in advance. The Friends of Outer Island facilitate visitation by the public, as well as host special events. Hours of operation for the public are weekends from June to the end of September. A maximum of 30 people can be on the island at one time and access is on a first-to-arrive basis. The schedule is subject to change without notice. The dock is not available for visiting boats so engine-powered vessels must moor offshore. There is a small beach for paddle-vessel landings. There is also a water taxi service that leaves from Stony Creek. Educational groups may visit the island by appointment only. See the Center for Education and Research at the Outer Island web site for more information.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Old Lyme Ferry Road Launch Site and Dock
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Launch car-top boats  at this site providing direct access to the Connecticut River.  Old Lyme Ferry Road Launch Site and Dock offers a small car-top boat access with floating dock and a very small beach area for wading.  Visitors may also picnic at this site.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: The property provides visual access only to Gatchen Creek, a tributary to the Menunketesuck River.  It offers excellent views and birding opportunities along a salt marsh including the adjacent 247-acre Salt Meadow Refuge Unit of the Stewart B. McKinney National Wildlife Refuge.

After being closed for nearly two decades, Pleasure Beach re-opened to the public in 2014 with free on-street parking. The peninsula is accessible seven days a week, except during inclement weather, via free water taxi from the fishing pier at 91 Seaview Ave. Upon arrival at the T-Pier on Pleasure Beach, it’s a half-mile walk along a boardwalk to the beach area. A free golf cart ride is available to take people from the boat to the beach. Please keep in mind that this park contains rare plants. Visitors should stay on desginated foot paths. Please call the Parks Department at (203) 576-7233 to find out more information and details regarding the water taxi schedule. Visit the Park website for additional details.

Pleasure Beach offers approximately 100 feet of Long Island Sound beach frontage with beautiful views of Long Island Sound. Park at the nearby Dock Road State Boat Launch north of the beach or the New Shore Road parking area 100’ from entrance where parking pass are required and sold at the Town Recreation & Parks office. Pleasure Beach closes at dusk. Lifeguards on duty, conditions permitting, during the summer season.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: Rober Sisca c/o Cannfield Associates LLC
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This small cove-side subdivision with on-site parking for public use of a small car-top boat launch and public viewing area includes a tidal wetland restoration area.

Public access waterfront walkway that runs in front of the Riverwatch Condominiums. This walkway connects to other public walkways to the North (in front of the Uhaul commercial building) and South (the Wastewater Treatment Plant Waterfront Walkway). Enjoy some beautiful views of the Norwalk River and all the wildlife it attracts!
This coastal access site has a beautiful walkway which follows the Norwalk River.

Visitors to this site can enjoy views of the Thames River from a bench provided by Garbo Lobster.  This public access site is located at the top of an escarpment providing fine views of vessels navigating busy New London Harbor and is a short walk to Fort Griswold State Park.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Elizabeth B. Karter Watch Rock Preserve
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Located at the mouth of Duck River near Great Island, this a 25-acre Old Lyme Land Trust property hosts a variety of habitat types.  Broadleaf forest, a conifer grove, open field,vernal pool, brackish marsh and creek, and rocky shoreline occupy the site's  nearly level to slightly undulating terraubs, and the rocky shoreline offers views across tidal marshlands towards Great Island, the Connecticut River and Long Island Sound. A small loop trail  takes visitors to Duck River and then back around to the point of Watch Rock. No trash receptacles are provided at the park, so please, carry-out what you carry-in. In order to protect this site's sensitive natural resources, no fires are allowed within the Preserve.

This salt marsh estuarine system lies along Birch Plain Creek and offers an excellent habitat for a variety of animals.  A gravel parking lot is provided and there are nice walking trails along the creek.
This site includes a concrete public access walkway along the Branford River. Park in the spaces designated as public parking for this site, and enjoy a nice stroll down the walkway to the water!

This 200-foot long walkway along Shaw Cove was developed as part of the neighboring condominium complex and will link the City of New London's waterfront park at the City Pier with the Fort Trumbull Riverwalk in the future.  Currently, the walkway provides only visual access to New London Harbor (and Shaw Cove) in the vicinity of the condominium development.  A hurricane barrier protects this site, which separates the condominium development from the public access facility.  Access to the public area is via Sparyard Street.

Gaps in the concrete on the groin at this site that traditionally have provided angler access to the waters at Woodmont Beach create extreme safety hazards, especially at high tide when the groin is over-topped by water. These conditions now restrict water access at this site from the beach only.   Park on side streets off of Beach Avenue, not on Beach Avenue, to access this site.

The waterfront walkway along Cos Cobb Harbor at this small office building is within a larger commercial complex. It provides an intimate space to enjoy views of the Harbor.  Follow the signed walkways along either the north or south side of the building to access the waterfront. Two parking spaces are reserved for visitors to the site's waterfront access area.

This site offers a view of the Morris Creek Preserve's salt marsh.  Access to the creek is restricted by vegetation for the most part, however some areas might accommodate a closer look at creek.  The preserve is located within a residential neighborhood, and visitors are relegated to parking along the street on a relatively narrow city road.  There is also parking on a small patch of mowed grass on Meadow View Rd across from residents.

From the Avery Tract visitors can hike trails near the Thames River and enjoy views of this important estuary.  Visitors should keep in mind that at the end of the red trail (described on The Avery Tract), they can step out of the woods and enjoy views of the River, but due to increased security measures at the nearby U.S. Submarine Base, it is crucial for visitors not to linger in the area, and they should definitely not take pictures!  Parking is available for approximately eight vehicles on either side of Scotch Cap Road (right before the crest of a hill).  There are signs on-site for the Waterford Land Trust and for hiking trails, and map boxes exist as well.  Use of motorized vehicles on the trails is prohibited, and hunting, trapping, tree cutting, and fires are also prohibited.
 
Multiple trails exist on this property, and cover an area much larger than what one observes upon approaching the entrance on Scotch Cap Road.  The woods abut railroad tracks, which, in turn, abut the Thames River.  As such, the property gives visual access to the river, but does not abut the river itself, so please do not cross the railroad tracks to attempt to physically access the river.  Visitors should follow marked trees to remain on-path, and proper footwear attire is necessary, in order to traverse rocky, unimproved trails.  Please check out waterfordlandtrust.org for more information about the site.
This  2.4 acre Town park on the Thames River offers a handicapped accessible walkway, benches, and picnic tables.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Mianus River Fishway at the River House Adult Day Center
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This site offers views of the Mianus River Dam and one of the most active diadromous fishways in Connecticut. The public can enjoy views of the river from benches in a small garden marked with the public access sign. The fishway access walk is open to the public throughout the spring migration (late March to June) and by appointment throughout the remainder of the year for educational purposes.

Access to this site consists of a seating patio and walkway along the waterfront. In all, this coastal access site has 250 linear feet of frontage along the water. Hours of operation are dawn to dusk.

200 feet of stone dust path atop a coastal bluff provides sweeping views of Long Island Sound at this site. Best to access this site by foot or bike (bike rack provided) due to limited on-site parking. Please respect the privacy of adjacent property owners and avoid sitting on the fences that separate the public from the private portions of the site.

This 1 mile waterfront walkway offers inspiring views of Niantic Bay and Long Island Sound. The entrance to this access site is located at Cini Park and the Hole-in-the-Wall beach. An opening in the boardwalks provides a small beach to rest in the sand. Use the East Lyme Public Trust Foundation's web cam at www.publictrustfoundation.org/webcam.htm to access live views of the the boardwalk. To help you reach this site follow the brown and white Long Island Sound Access signs.

This small undeveloped informal access site at the north end of Shore Avenue is located between the street and South Cove. Use of the site is limited to viewing South Cove from a small paved area. Although it is possible to launch a canoe/kayak at high tide, limited water depths and dense vegetation restrict boating access and may strand boaters in mud flats a low tide.
The site has a bench for seating.  Vegetation restricts the view from spring through fall.  Easy pedestrian access is available via the Route 1/Route 154 Intersection.
Enjoy a picnic lunch overlooking the Oyster River marsh at this  "neighborhood-scale" street-end coastal access site with benches.

A creative re-use of a five-acre former industrial property adjacent to Stonington Harbor has transformed this once-blighted industrial site into a unique waterfront residential community offering coastal public access.  Visitors are welcome to stroll the site's 800-foot long waterfront  path, observe vessels plying this busy harbor from the shade of a waterfront gazebo, or fish from a nearby breakwater accessed from this site.  Although the pedestrian access path is open 1/2 hour before sunrise to 1/2 hour after sunset, anglers may access the breakwater via the public walkway at the south end of the site at anytime. Due to the  proximity of this walkway to residences, it is important that anglers accessing the breakwater after sunset do so in a manner that will not disturb the site's residents.  Transient vessels anchored in Stonington Harbor may use the site's dinghy dock to access Stonington Borough. The dinghy dock  is open to the general public who wish to access the Borough from the Harbor and is NOT restricted to members of the Stonington Yacht Club who manage this facility.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Stony Creek Town Dock and Beach
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This coastal access point offers a variety of recreational opportunities within intimate-scale park facilities. Enjoy fine views of the Sound and Thimble Islands. Arrive early on summer weekends as on street parking is extremely limited. At this location you will also find the launch site for the Thimble Island tours which are open to the public.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Mystic River Dinghy Dock and Viewing Area
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This site provides dinghy access to downtown Mystic for transient boaters on the Mystic River (no overnight dinghy tie-ups allowed!). A bench at the site provides a quiet place to relax and enjoy views of the Mystic River. Limited parking on Holmes Street is available. Additional parking is available on Frazier and Forsyth Streets and at the 4th District Voting Hall located at 10 Broadway Ave. Site accessible for handicapped via a curb cut about 150-200 ft down the sidewalk.

The site provides an improved walkway connecting Fort Trumbull State Park to the railroad bridge at the entrance to Shaw Cove. Future plans for the walkway to span Shaw Cove would provide a pedestrian connection to City Pier and Waterfront Park. Benches, lighting, and monuments complement the walkway serving the Fort Trumbull peninsula which hosts one of the few remaining New London-Groton area commericial fishing vessel clusters.
This site provides unimproved access to the lower Connecticut River.  Park on the left (downstream) side of this road-ending, being careful not to park on the neighboring landowner's property.

Crushed mussel shell paths lead to the pond at two locations for visual access and passive recreational activities such as observing birds and other wildlife. The site is comprised of a wooded area with trails overlooking a pond believed to be tidally influenced and is near the Hammonasset River (and may be a tributary of the Hammonasset). Visitor hours are from sunrise until sunset.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: The Sound School Pier and Walkway
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This site, comprised of a pier and adjacent stone-dust pathway (on the developed shorefront), provides spectacular views of New Haven Harbor.  Visitors are able to enjoy the vista and may utilize the pier for fishing activities.  Parking is available at The Sound School lot at the end of Sea Street only after 3 p.m. or when school is not in session. Street parking is limted.

Also known as Rattlesnake Hill, this site is accessed by by a municipally owned right-of-way. Use the stairway at the corner of Palmer Street and Riverview Avenue down an escarpment to access to a small beach along Mystic Harbor. Parking is available at Town owned open space across from the house at Town-owned open space across from house at 66 Riverview Ave in Noank.

Mill Pond is a municipally owned park in Westport.  Parking and car top boat launch access is available to non-residents October through April but restricted to Town residents May through September.  Permits issued only to residents of Westport.  Non-residents may launch year-round at the nearby Saugatuck River State Boat Launch . The general public may park at metered parking spots (1 hour parking) on Hillspoint Road to access the site when on-site parking is restricted to residents only. Tide gates on Mill Pond do not provide boating access to Long Island Sound.

The Selden Creek Preserve trail  passes through a towering mixed forest to a scenic overlook that provides opportunities to view a variety of birdlife along Selden Creek and tidal marshes including roosting bald eagles. The Preserve takes the name of the creek that divides it from the 600-acre Selden Island State Park. The Preserve includes wetlands that are part of a large wetland complex within the lower Connecticut River recognized as having conservation value of international importance pursuant to the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands, an intergovernmental treaty dedicated to the conservation and wise use of wetlands.
Stone dust surface pedestrian path along Indian River tidal marshes.

Small unimproved area provides access to sandy beach at approximately 110 Trolley Rd. Walk only along the beach below the wet sandy mark after entering the site to remain within the area open to the public. To access the site park in the dirt parking lot at the end of Trolley road at CT DEEP Great Harbor Wildlife Management Area dirt parking lot and then walk back along Trolley Road approximately 200 yards. Entrance to the site is on the right from the parking area.

This small neighborhod-scale  passive recreation area offers fine views of an inlet within Baker Cove.  A  picnic area with seating provides a pleasant venue for enjoying an afternoon along the cove.  A parking area and stone dust paths provide easy access to site's amenities. Look for the gravel drive entrance to the site opposite Plant Street and adjacent to a small brown sewer pump staition. The site is located directly across Baker Cove from the Elks Lodge.  Launching of small boats from this site is not recommended since low tide leaves the waters too shallow. Use the nearby Bayberry Lane State Boat Launch instead to launch your small boat to paddle Baker Cove.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: Borough of Fenwick c/o Larry DeBlasiis
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Enjoy a quiet walk in a unique remnant oak-beech-sassafras coastal forest along South Cove at Fenwick Gove. Approximately 2 miles of trails includes views of South Cove and coastal grassland meadow. PLEASE keep dogs on leash.

The Hammocks residential subdivision provides a public access path providing visual access to the Hammock River, tidal marshes, and outer Clinton Harbor. Parking area for public access path is on Beach Park Road opposite Holland Drive.

Pinkney Historic Park is located adjacent to the headquarters of the Rowayton Historic Society.  Visitors can enjoy fine views of the Five Mile River and then a walk through the village of Rowayton lined with shops and eateries.  This district of Norwalk also often has concerts and special events in the center of the park.  There is no parking on the site, however visitors may park on the street within the center of Rowayton.

Among the most recent additions to Connecticut's shoreline municipal parks, this handsome outdoor recreation facility is the former site of the Cos Cob Power Plant. Purchased from the State of Connecticut for $1, the formerly contaminated industrial property was remediated to provide the general public with a variety of outdoor recreational amenities including 0.8 miles of walkways, a paviilion and playgrounds, all within view of Cos Cob Harbor.

This site offers wildlife observation opportunities within a shallow water cove on the Mystic River. A small non-motorized car-top boating access facility provides to the River at low tide. However, be sure to consult a tide schedule before planning to use the launch to avoid being stranded in tidal mudflats at low water! When accessing the water from the parking area, stay on the right side of the path to avoid disturbing neighboring residential property owners where "No Trespassing" signs may be posted. Access the site's small unpaved parking area by turning into the site's access driveway adjacent to a Town of Stonington sanitary pump station facility. Proceed approximately 100 feet to site's waterfront.

Enjoy fabulous views of Bridgeport Harbor and nearby Pleasure Beach at this fishing access pier. Visitors can also take a free water taxi from the pier to Pleasure Beach. Please call the Parks Department at (203) 576-7233 to find out more information and details regarding the water taxi schedule.
A gravel path within residential subdivision provides visual access only to the Ragged Rock Creek marsh.

This handicapped accessible walkway along the Norwalk River provides visual access only to the Norwalk River. Free parking across street at Norwalk City Hall is available if no parking is available on-site.

Clinton Landing, a small town-owned park along a tidal segment of the Indian River, is located behind the Town Hall. A gazebo, observation platform, dock, boardwalk and interpretive sign describing the area’s wildlife provide a variety of ways to enjoy the serenity of the River.

This nearly 600-acre property, acquired by the Town of Guilford in 2009, offers a variety of coastal habitats along a tidal segment of the East River. Footpaths and old logging roads provide access throughout the property. The principal access area is located on Sullivan Drive off of Goose Lane at the Town’s brush/leaf disposal area. Enter the site’s fields here at the sign announcing the East River Preserve and be sure to park in an area reserved for visitors before crossing the bridge over the East River. The Clapboard Hill Road access offers the best views of the East River but provides more limited access to the property via a short loop trail. Three private residences reamain within a portion of the site along the fields nearest the Clapboard Road trailhead. Please respect this private landowner's privacy by staying on designated trails in this area and following all postings directing visitors to stay on the publicly-owned portions of the site.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Saltwater Farm Vineyard Car-top Boat Launch
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Views of a pristine saltwater marsh along Oxecossett Creek beckon from a canoe and kayak (only) boat launch. Paddle along the creek leads to Wequetequock Cove and DEEP’s Barn Island Wildlife Management Area 1/2 mile away. This former Stonington airfield off Route 1A was redeveloped as a vineyard and special events venue. It now hosts a car-top boat launch with parking for five vehicles located at the entrance to the vineyard. Look for the wine barrel at the entrance to Saltwater Farm Vineyards on Route 1A (near Route 1) and Long Island Sound public access signs. Follow the pathway to the launch from the parking area, and BE CAREFUL to time your launch and return to avoid low tide when the launch is extremely muddy/slippery.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: Hamilton Develoipment Corp. c/o James Donaher
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Enjoy a stroll along the scenic Saugatuck riverfront at this site! Visitors are restricted to enjoying views of the river from a public access boardwalk. Kayak and paddleboard rentals are available to the public from the on-site outfitter, Sea Kayak Connecticut. To find this site, look for the 'Sea Kayak Connecticut' paddlesport signage at the entrance to the commercial center. Parking is located on-site, in nearby public parking lots, and along Riverside Avenue. For information about rentals and tours, visit seakayakct.com. The routes leading from the sidewalk to the public access boardwalk are posted with brown and white 'Shoreline Public Access' signs.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: William R. Haase IV Memorial Canoe/Kayak Launch
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This small semi-improved launch provides non-motorized car-top boat access only to Poquetanuck Cove. The site does not support trailered-boat launching. Potentially hazardous conditions restrict use launch during high tide only. You MUST consult a tide chart for predicted water elevations for the Thames River before using this launch, or  risk launching or landing your boat in deep mud. An interpretive sign at this site describes the ecology of the Cove and its tidal marshes.

This small parklet located between #422 and #446 Riverdale Drive provides access to the coastal waters and sandy beach between Short Beach and Stratford Point. Anglers may use the site until 10 pm to access the waters off Stratford Point. Please respect the privacy of adjacent landowners when using this walkway to access  coastal waters, especially during  evening hours. Your QUIET enjoyment of this pathway to coastal waters will help ensure that it remains open to all during early evening hours.

This neighborhood scale preserve in the village of Stony Creek on Jarvis Creek and Long Island Sound offers fine views of the Thimble Islands. The preserve contains coastal forest, tidal marsh, a small old field, an old quarry pit and other relics of the area’s quarry industry. Pedestrian only trails access most of the preserve and provide vistas of the creek, marsh and Long Island Sound. Bicycles are not allowed.  A boardwalk crosses the marsh to a small island and an old tide gate. The trail continues from this point onto an adjacent preserve on the east side of Jarvis Creek. Check Branford Land Trust website, brandfordlandtrust.org for maps and more information. There is an unimproved area for parking two cars on the left side of Buena Vista Road immediately after where the paved road ends. Ignore the 'No Tresspassing'  sign posted near the entrance to the site. The Land Trust's access easement along this roadway provides legal pedestrian access to the Preserve's trails.  Parking is also available on nearby Thimble Island Road.

A former general aviation airport, Salt Meadow Park now hosts recreation fields and conservation lands with coastal grasslands, coastal forest and saltmarsh. Stroll footpaths along the edge the ball fields with views of the Hammonasset River marsh. The footpath leads to trails within small patch of coastal forest with a rock bluff offering fine views of Long Island Sound.

Selden's Landing provides unimproved access to Selden's Cove for passive recreation only. Shallow water and tidal wetlands along the shoreline limit public use to the site's upland. The upland area offers wildlife observation opportunities and views of the Selden Cove. Due to these and other site constraints, Selden Landing is NOT available for launching small craft. Car-top boat access to the Cove is available from the Hadlyme Ferry boat launch approximately 1/2 nautical miles upstream on the Connecticut River at 154 Ferry Road, Lyme, CT) . See https://portal.ct.gov/DEEP/Boating/Boat-Launches/Hadlyme-Ferry-Boat-Launch for more on this launch. Steep slopes from Selden Road to the site's waterfront and lack of a well-defined path may limit safe access to the site's waterfront by those with mobility impairments.

Crescent Beach Walkway is a 300-yard stone dust path atop a bluff overlooking beautiful Niantic Bay. Both the northern and southern ends of the walkway terminate at Crescent Beach. On-street parking is available, where permitted, on Crescent Avenue near its intersection with Carpenter Avenue.

An access pier over the water at this marina provides views of Branford Harbor. Three parking spaces are reserved for vistors adjacent to the access pier, which is located adjacent to the marina's travel lift. Open dawn to dusk.
Visitors can enjoy views of the Lieutenant River and wetlands beside a café. Two parking spaces are provided next to the restaurant parking lot.

Enjoy a beautiful day at this peaceful, 6-acre site overlooking the western side of Sherwood Mill Pond. Donated to Aseptuck Land Trust in 1984, the preserve does not have trails but offers a great opportunity for wildlife viewing. Tread carefully, as there is lots of interesting and environmentally beneficial salt marsh vegetation that grows here! Parking is limited to a small on-street section of Grove Point, along the edge of the preserve - do not block the private residences located along the street. This site is open from sunrise to sunset.
Waterview Park offers a large grassy field, picnic tables and views of the waterfront.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Mamacoke Conservation Area at Connecticut College Arboretum
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc:
Mamacoke is a designated natural area within the Connecticut College Arboretum. The rocky and wooded 40-acre island in the Thames River is attached to the mainland by a small tidal saltmarsh. The National Audubon Society has recognized the shoreline of the Thames River between Harrison’s Landing and Smith Cove in Quaker Hill (Waterford) as an Important Bird Area for Connecticut. The brackish water of the Thames River generally does not freeze completely and thus provides an open-water refuge for several waterfowl species. Other than trail maintenance, this area remains as undisturbed by human activity as possible.

Written directions to access Mamacoke Island from the parking area are difficult to follow. Please consult the interactive and printable maps available on the Arboretum’s website. The Trail Map shows marked walking trails. Mamacoke is mapped in pink though the actual blazes on the island are white.

Take a walk on trails through fields of wildflowers with expansive views of Long Island Sound. Knox Preserve is an excellent destination for bird watching, especially its colony of purple martins. Please use only established trails, do not cross the railroad tracks and respect nearby private property. Parking is along the north side of Wilcox Rd. Do not block the entrance to the preserve.

Formerly called Daniel Avenue Beach, Barbara Pine Memorial Beach was renamed in 2017. Swimming is not feasible during low tide, but can be done (unsupervised) during other times of the day. Barbara Pine is a beautiful little coastal gem located not far from Chittenden Park, and has some great views of Long Island Sound. There is no fee to use this site and visitors should park in the designated dirt lot or find on-street parking. Dogs are allowed.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Sluice Creek Car Top Boat Launch
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Cartop (only) boat launch from this site provides great access to the Sluice Creek Marsh. Access the site via Dock Lane off of Seaview Terrace near intersection with Whitfield Street. Park in lot on left after passing Oceanco building on right.

The Tidal Marsh Trail (TMT) is a half-mile hiking trail, located off Universal Drive N in North Haven, CT, that follows the eastern shore of the Quinnipiac River. The trail is fairly level, well-maintained, and features some unique views of the river and its wetlands. It also offers an opportunity for outdoor activities ranging from bird watching, to fishing, to canoeing and kayaking. The site is clearly marked and accessible behind the Target located on Universal Drive N. in North Haven, CT. There is one sign along the drive that points individuals towards trail head. Dogs are allowed on-leash and biking is permitted. This trail is maintained by the North Haven Trail Association.

ctparks_coastal_v1.ownerName: CT Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: This State wildlife management area provides unimproved access to the Menunketesuck River and Chapman Mill Pond. DO NOT ACCESS THE DERELICT FOOTBRIDGE to cross the River. It is unsafe. Accessing this structure risks serious injury. Fishing is prohibited within 250 feet downstream of the dam and 20 feet upstream.
This site provides water access along a walkway adjacent to the Red 36 Restaurant and the pier at the end of Cottrell Street next to a boat yard. Limited street parking is located nearby.
Neighborhood-scale water access with views of Mystic Seaport and car-top boat access to the Mystic River. Parking on Park Place is extremely limted. Best to park on nearby streets where allowed.

ctparks_coastal_v1.n: Central Hall Block Mystic River Access
ctparks_coastal_v1.desc: Walkway over Mystic River behind Central Hall Building. Access walkway via Gravel Street entrance at Pump Station.

Enjoy a short scenic stroll to a large viewing platform right on the water! Though the dock is private, this viewing area offers up some cool sights. The entrance to the walkway is delineated by a brown and white 'Public Access' sign. Access is open from dawn to dusk, and public parking is available in the site's residential lot (it is marked by a 'Public Access Parking' sign). Please do not park in undesignated spots.

The Steelpointe Harborwalk runs from The Bass Pro Shops, along the scenic Bridgeport Harbor, and loops in front of Boca Oyster Bar. The Steelpointe Development features some awesome selections for entertainment, dining and retail - easily accessible before, during or after your stroll. The marina itself boasts 200+ slips and is easily viewed from the harborwalk. Bicycles and skateboards are not allowed, but bring your dogs (leashed, of course)! This site is open daily from 8AM-8PM.

This site offers limited views of a salt marsh from a waterfront gazebo. The entrance to the condominiums indicates the site is private property but the public can enter to use coastal access site. After entering take a left, then follow the road to its terminus, then take a right and park at end the road adjacent to the gazebo.
